# learner


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

This module is the base of the engine. Every other module imports from
it, and it imports from no other module of abhyasa. It holds what
abhyasa knows about the learner, and the shelf where it keeps it. The
parts come in the order that they import each other:

- **Settings**: the settings file, the settings table and its defaults.
- **Prompts**: the system prompts that you can see and change in
  Settings.
- **The store**: the learning shelf in your vault. Each concept, attempt
  and session is one document.
- **The learner model**: the depth, the floor and the ceiling of each
  concept, and when to review it.
- **Ways to learn**: which way of teaching helps you, such as code or an
  analogy.
- **The profile**: your background, goals, interests and pace.
- **Background jobs**: the stored rows of the jobs that the activity
  chip shows.
- **Stored walks**: read and save a walk, find its current idea, and
  count its steps.

Two functions of the profile ask a model. They import the model layer
(`abhyasa.models`) when they run, because that layer imports this
module.

Import the modules that this module uses. The heavy ones load inside the
functions that need them, so the import stays light.

## Settings

One table for each value that you can change, and the file that keeps
your changes.

Each value that a person can change is a row in one table, `SETTINGS`. A
row has a group, a name, a label, one line of help, a type, a default
and, for a number, a range. The engine, the web app and the Settings
page all read this table. Thus each value has one place.

Your changes go in `settings.json` in
[`cfg_dir()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#cfg_dir).
The code reads a value when it uses it, so a change works at once, with
no restart. A saved value outside its range gets the nearest end of the
range. A saved value of the wrong type gets the default. A bad file
never stops the app.

This module imports only the standard library and fastcore. Each engine
module reads its values from here, so the import must stay light.

### The groups

The Settings page shows the groups in this order. Each group has a label
and one lead line.

### The table

[`add`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#add) puts one
row in `SETTINGS`. The name is `section.key`: the section of
`settings.json` and the key in it. The type comes from the default.
`more` puts the row under the closed “More” part of its group.
`store='profile'` marks a value that the vault keeps in your profile,
not this file. `hi` can be the name of another row. Then that value is
the top of the range. `ui=False` marks a value that its group shows with
its own controls. `reset=False` keeps a value when you use the defaults
of its group: the theme, and the speech engine and model.

### add

``` python
def add(
    name:str, group:str, label:str, help:str, dflt, lo:NoneType=None, hi:NoneType=None, more:bool=False,
    choices:NoneType=None, unit:str='', pct:bool=False, store:str='file', ui:bool=True, reset:bool=True
):
```

*Add the setting `name` to `SETTINGS` and return its row.*

The **Look** group keeps its own controls: the theme swatches and the
mode. The **Learning** group holds the three values of your profile.

The **Walks** group sets the size of a walk and of a side walk.

The **Talks** group sets how a talk runs: the questions, the time, the
vote and the room.

The **Checks and grading** group sets the tries, the grade of a shaky
pass, and when an idea counts as learned.

The **Review** group sets the time to the next review. A daily limit on
review is new: 0 means no limit, as before.

The **Links** group sets how much of a link the tutor gets. The pages
read by default can not be more than the page cap.

The **Research** group sets the web search for a step with no source.
The tutor searches the web for the idea, reads the best pages, and
quotes one passage word for word. When research is off, the tutor does
no web search, and the step says that the text is in the tutor’s words.

The **Speech to text** group keeps the engine and the model, and the
pauses at which the mic cuts what you say. The **Screen guide** group
has the voice and the look of a point mark. A point mark is weaker than
a circle in each look, so a circle is always the main mark of a step.
The default is `tick`, because it has no ring that looks like a circle.

The **Speaking voice** group picks who reads the steps of the screen
guide aloud. `pocket` runs Pocket TTS on this Mac. `openai` sends each
line to OpenAI. `browser` is the voice of the browser (or of the Mac in
the overlay). The `voice` module reads these values. The default is
`pocket`. Until its model is downloaded, the browser speaks. An old `hf`
or `kokoro` value is not one of the choices, so it reads as `pocket`.
The speed is only for OpenAI: Pocket TTS has no speed.

The **Models** group has the default model and one model for each task.
An empty value uses the default model. The tasks after
[`extract`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/sources.html#extract)
borrow the model of an older task when they have none: `BORROWS` says
which. The screen guide (`guide`) and its figure labels (`guide_vision`)
use the model for hints until you pick one. The builder chat (`build`)
is an agent: it uses the default model until you pick one, and it has no
reply cap. The reply caps are in tokens.

The **Lists** group sets how many items show in the lists of the app.
All of it is under “More”.

Each group except **Prompts** has rows, and each row is in a group. The
Prompts group lists the prompts of `prompts.PROMPTS`.

``` python
assert set(GROUPS) - {'prompts'} == {r.group for r in SETTINGS.values()}
assert all(r.kind != 'int' or r.lo <= r.dflt for r in SETTINGS.values())
len(SETTINGS)
```

### The file

`DFLT_SETTINGS` is the default of each section: the rows that the file
keeps, the saved prompt texts and the models that the Settings page
downloaded.
[`settings()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#settings)
gives the saved settings over the defaults. A section that is not a dict
in the file is ignored, and a top-level key that is not known is
dropped.

### cfg_dir

``` python
def cfg_dir()->pathlib.Path:
```

*The folder for abhyasa’s settings and keys: the one of
[`use_config`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#use_config),
else `$ABHYASA_CONFIG`, else `~/.config/abhyasa`.*

[`use_config`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#use_config)
gives a host its own folder for the files that abhyasa keeps: the
settings, the session key and the caches. A context variable holds it,
so a standalone abhyasa in the same process still uses
`$ABHYASA_CONFIG`.
[`CtxPool`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#ctxpool)
jobs and `copy_context` threads see the folder of the call that started
them.

``` python
own = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
test_eq(is_hosted(), False)
with use_config(own): test_eq((cfg_dir(), is_hosted()), (own, True))
with use_config(None): test_eq(is_hosted(), False)
with use_config(own): ctx = contextvars.copy_context()
test_eq(ctx.run(cfg_dir), own)
test_ne(cfg_dir(), own)
```

A host sets context variables for one request, such as the settings of
[`use_settings`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#use_settings)
or the workspace of the caller.
[`CtxPool`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#ctxpool)
is a thread pool whose jobs run in a copy of the context of the call
that submitted them, so a job in the background sees the same values.

<a

target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### CtxPool

``` python
def CtxPool(
    max_workers:NoneType=None, thread_name_prefix:str='', initializer:NoneType=None, initargs:tuple=()
):
```

*A thread pool whose jobs run in a copy of the submitter’s context.*

A value set before `submit` is seen by the job, also through `map`. A
value set after is not.

``` python
v = contextvars.ContextVar('v', default='none')
with CtxPool(1) as p:
    tok = v.set('mine')
    test_eq(p.submit(v.get).result(), 'mine')
    test_eq(list(p.map(lambda _: v.get(), [0])), ['mine'])
    v.reset(tok)
    test_eq(p.submit(v.get).result(), 'none')
```

[`_saved`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#_saved)
reads the file only when it changed, so a value read in a loop costs one
`stat`.

### save_settings

``` python
def save_settings(
    d:dict
)->dict:
```

*Write all the settings. In
[`use_settings`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#use_settings)
the host owns the values, so a write is refused.*

With no file,
[`settings()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#settings)
gives the defaults. A change in one section keeps the others.

``` python
test_eq(settings()['walks']['steps'], 7)
update_settings('stt', segment=False)
test_eq(settings()['stt']['segment'], False)
test_eq(settings()['look'], dict(theme='paper', mode='auto', keys_float=True))
update_settings('stt', segment=True)
```

A file from before this table still loads: its sections update the
defaults, and the new sections get their defaults.

``` python
_path().write_text(json.dumps(dict(stt=dict(engine='mlx', model='m', segment=True), models=dict(question='', grade='', hint='', lesson=''),
                                   tokens=dict(question='', grade='', hint='', lesson='', extract=''), look=dict(theme='ink', mode='dark'), prompts={}, downloaded=[])))
d = settings()
test_eq((d['stt']['engine'], d['stt']['pause'], d['look']['theme'], d['walks']['steps'], d['models']['extract']), ('mlx', 700, 'ink', 7, ''))
save_settings(dict(prompts={}, downloaded=[]))
```

A file that is not JSON, or a section that is not a dict, gives the
defaults. An unknown top-level key is dropped.

``` python
_path().write_text('{not json')
test_eq(settings()['walks']['steps'], 7)
_path().write_text(json.dumps(dict(walks=5, mine=1)))
d = settings()
test_eq((d['walks']['steps'], 'mine' in d), (7, False))
save_settings(dict(prompts={}, downloaded=[]))
```

### Read one value

[`fit`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#fit) makes a
saved value fit its row. A number outside the range gets the nearest
end. A value of the wrong type gets the default. A whole number can come
as `12.0` from a form; it stays a whole number. A choice must be one of
the choices.

### raw

``` python
def raw(
    name:str
):
```

*The saved value of `name` as it is in the file, or None.*

[`use_settings`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#use_settings)
gives a host its own values for the rows that the file keeps, for the
code inside one `with`. The host passes
[`rows`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#rows): the
row name (`'walks.steps'`) to its value. A name that is not a file row
is dropped. Each value still goes through
[`fit`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#fit), so a
number outside the range or a value of the wrong type is made to fit. A
row that the host does not give has its default, and the file is not
read. A context variable holds the rows, so another thread, or a later
call, does not see them. `rows=None` changes nothing.

### use_settings

``` python
def use_settings(
    rows:dict | None
):
```

*Read [`rows`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#rows)
(row name to value) instead of the settings file, for this call only;
`None` keeps what is in use.*

A given value is used inside the `with` and not after it. It is made to
fit its row, and a name that is not a row is dropped. A saved value in
the file does not show inside the `with`.

``` python
update_settings('walks', steps=5)
with use_settings({'walks.steps': 99, 'walks.note': 30, 'nope.x': 1, 'prompts.x': 2}):
    inside = (val('walks.steps'), val('walks.note'), val('walks.chain'), settings()['walks']['steps'])
with use_settings(None): none = val('walks.steps')
update_settings('walks', steps=7)
test_eq((inside, none, val('walks.steps')), ((7, 30, dflt('walks.chain'), 99), 5, 7))   # `val` fits a value to its row; `settings()` keeps the raw value, as it does for the file
```

`sources.roots` is a text list, one path for each line. A source folder
has the same rules as a folder that you name: it must be in your home
folder, it must not be the home folder itself, and no part of it can be
hidden or a link.
[`source_root_why`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#source_root_why)
gives the reason when a path breaks a rule.
[`roots`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#roots)
gives the paths that keep the rules, and
[`dropped_roots`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#dropped_roots)
gives the others with their reasons, so the Settings page can show them.

A saved 50 ideas becomes 7, the most. A string gives the default. A
share above 1 becomes 1.

``` python
update_settings('walks', steps=50, hands='a lot', note=40.0)
test_eq((val('walks.steps'), val('walks.hands'), val('walks.note')), (7, 1/3, 40))
update_settings('walks', hands=1.5, steps=1)
test_eq((val('walks.hands'), val('walks.steps')), (1., 3))
save_settings(dict(prompts={}, downloaded=[]))
```

The top of the pages read by default is the page cap.

``` python
update_settings('links', pages=40, cap=10)
test_eq((val('links.pages'), val('links.cap')), (10, 10))
save_settings(dict(prompts={}, downloaded=[]))
```

The look of a point mark is one of three choices. A look that is not a
choice gives the default, `tick`.

``` python
update_settings('guide', point='dot')
test_eq(val('guide.point'), 'dot')
update_settings('guide', point='arrow')
test_eq((val('guide.point'), SETTINGS['guide.point'].choices), ('tick', ('tick', 'dot', 'ring')))
save_settings(dict(prompts={}, downloaded=[]))
```

### Change one value

[`set_val`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#set_val)
saves a value made to fit its row, and returns it.
[`reset`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#reset) puts
back the default of one row, and
[`reset_group`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#reset_group)
of each row in a group.
[`changed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#changed)
is true when a value is not its default.
[`clamped`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#clamped)
gives the value in the file when it was outside the range, so the page
can say so.

### set_val

``` python
def set_val(
    name:str, v
):
```

*Save the value `v` of the setting `name`, made to fit its row. Return

The source folders drop the root of the disk, the home folder itself and
a hidden folder.

``` python
set_val('sources.roots', '/\n~\n~/.ssh\n~/code/personal/orgs\n')
test_eq(roots(), ['~/code/personal/orgs'])
test_eq([l for l, _ in dropped_roots()], ['/', '~', '~/.ssh'])
reset('sources.roots')
```

A value saved out of range is saved as the end of the range.
[`reset`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#reset) and
[`reset_group`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#reset_group)
put back the defaults.

``` python
test_eq(set_val('walks.steps', 99), 7)
test_eq(set_val('walks.steps', 1), 3)
test_eq(raw('walks.steps'), 3)
assert changed('walks.steps') and not changed('walks.note')
reset('walks.steps')
test_eq(val('walks.steps'), 7)
set_val('checks.tries', 5); set_val('checks.near', 8)
test_eq(sorted(reset_group('checks')), ['checks.near', 'checks.tries'])
test_eq((val('checks.tries'), val('checks.near')), (3, 7))
update_settings('walks', steps=50)
test_eq(clamped('walks.steps'), 50)
# a number typed by hand as text works, and text that is not a number gives the default
update_settings('tokens', hint='900', grade='many')
test_eq((val('tokens.hint'), val('tokens.grade')), (900, 2048))
# a value that the profile keeps has no reset here
test_fail(lambda: reset('learning.pace'), contains='profile')
save_settings(dict(prompts={}, downloaded=[]))
```

The speaking engine is `browser` until you change it, and a value that
is not an engine gives the default.

``` python
test_eq((val('voice.out'), val('voice.out_speed')), ('pocket', 1.))
test_eq((fit(SETTINGS['voice.out'], 'kokoro'), fit(SETTINGS['voice.out'], 'hf')), ('pocket', 'pocket'))
```

### What stays fixed

Some values keep you safe, so they have no setting: the link checks for
local addresses, plain HTTP, the link kinds, the HTML allowlist, the
check of a pane address, the local-only hosts, the test allowlist, the
grade scale and the depth ladder. The room for phones keeps its safety
limits fixed too: the bind rule, the join code, the rate limits, the
body size and the headers. `FIXED` names them, and no row may have one
of these words in its name.

``` python
assert not [n for n in SETTINGS for w in FIXED if w in n]
```

## Prompts

The instruction text of the tutor. You can change it on the Settings
page.

Each prompt of the tutor has two parts. The variable parts (the concept,
the thread, the JSON shape) stay in code. The instruction text is in
this registry. Each prompt has a name, a plain label, a note on what it
changes, and its default text from code. The Settings page shows each
prompt, and you can change its text there. The tutor reads each prompt
when it calls the model. Thus a change works on the next question, with
no restart.

Import the tools that this module uses. The settings come from
[`settings`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#settings)
only when a prompt is read, so the import stays light.

### The registry

[`register`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#register)
adds a prompt to `PROMPTS` and returns its default text. A `check` can

### Tests

A small prompt with a check of 2 lines. Its default is in use at first.

``` python
register('greet', 'Greeting', 'The first line.', 'Say hello.\nSay your name.', need_lines(2, 'The greeting'))
test_eq(prompt('greet'), 'Say hello.\nSay your name.')
```

A saved text is in use at once, and the settings keep it under
`prompts`.

``` python
test_eq(set_prompt('greet', 'Say hi.\r\nSay your job.\n'), 'Say hi.\nSay your job.')
test_eq((prompt('greet'), saved()), ('Say hi.\nSay your job.', {'greet': 'Say hi.\nSay your job.'}))
```

A text that fails the check is refused with a plain message, and the
saved text stays.

``` python
test_fail(lambda: set_prompt('greet', 'Only one line.'), contains='needs 2 lines')
test_eq(prompt('greet'), 'Say hi.\nSay your job.')
```

An empty text, or only spaces, removes the saved text, so the default is
in use again. A text that is the same as the default is not kept.

``` python
test_eq(set_prompt('greet', '  \n '), 'Say hello.\nSay your name.')
set_prompt('greet', 'Say hello.\nSay your name.')
test_eq(saved(), {})
```

[`use_prompts`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#use_prompts)
gives a draft text to the code that runs inside its `with`, and to no
other call. The Try it button of Settings uses it, so the real reader
runs on the draft with no change. The saved text stays as it was.

``` python
with use_prompts(dict(greet='Say hi.')): inside = prompt('greet')
test_eq((inside, prompt('greet')), ('Say hi.', 'Say hello.\nSay your name.'))
```

An unknown name is an error. Then the test prompt goes away.

``` python
test_fail(lambda: prompt('nope'))
del PROMPTS['greet']
```

## The store

The `learning` shelf: concepts, attempts and sessions as vault
documents.

This module keeps all learning data in your vault, on one shelf named
`learning`. Each concept, attempt and session is one vault document.
Thus each tool that reads the vault can search it. The other modules
read and write the shelf only through the
[`Learning`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#learning)
class in this module.

Import the tools that this module uses, and the `Vault` class of the
vault.

### The shelf

Search reads the text of a document. The `meta` JSON keeps the state.
`Vault.set_meta` changes the state and does not embed the text again.
The table gives the source URI of each kind of document.

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>kind</th>
<th>source</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>concept</code></td>
<td><code>learning://concept/&lt;slug&gt;</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>attempt</code></td>
<td><code>learning://attempt/&lt;id&gt;</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>session</code></td>
<td><code>learning://session/&lt;id&gt;</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

These constants name the shelf, give the start state of a concept, and
list the fields that merge.

[`slugify`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#slugify)
makes the key of a concept from its name. It changes a name in an Indic
script, such as Devanagari, to IAST first. It changes `+`, `#` and `&`
to words, so C, C++ and C# get different slugs. A name with no letters
that it can read gets a short hash of the name. Thus the same name
always gives the same slug.
[`_src`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#_src) makes
the source URI of a document.

### Shelves of documents

A vault file holds more stores than the shelves of documents. For
example, the vault keeps the names that it finds in a store named
`entities`. That store has no `doc_id` column and no `docs` table.
vishalakshi’s `Vault.shelf_names` gives only the shelves that hold
documents. `doc_shelf` opens one of them with `shelf(create=False)`, or
gives None. It never makes a new shelf, so a name in a link or in an old
walk does not add a store to your vault.

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L537"

### Write concepts

`put` adds a concept or adds to it. It keeps the learner state, merges
the list fields and replaces the other fields. It does not change the
group of a concept that the learner moved by hand (see Groups below).
Two fields say what the learner must understand. `core` is the
understanding in 1 or 2 sentences: what the idea does and why. It has no
sizes, years or scores, unless the number is the idea. `wrong` lists 1
to 3 common wrong ideas, each as `{'think': ..., 'fact': ...}`. The
question and the grade work from these two fields. `statement` stays as
the reference text. An empty `core` or `wrong` keeps the old value.
[`wrong_ideas`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#wrong_ideas)
makes each wrong idea a dict.
[`clean_name`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#clean_name)
makes a name one line with no control characters, at most `NAME_LEN`
characters. `put` and `rename` use it.

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L580"

### Move old slugs

abhyasa 0.0.5 and older made slugs in a different way. A name in
Devanagari got a random slug, and C, C++ and C# got the same slug, `c`.
`reslug` finds each concept that has an old slug. It moves the concept
to the slug that
[`slugify`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#slugify)
gives now. It also changes the slug in each place that points to it: the
links of other concepts, attempts, sessions, walks and demos. A slug
that a source sets, such as `sa-term-karaka`, does not change.

`reslug` finds the moves first. With `dry_run` it stops there and writes
nothing.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L648"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
    dry_run:bool=False

```

[`slugify`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#slugify),
and every slug that points to it. Returns `{old: new}`.*

### Groups

A concept can sit in a group under its subject. For example, Magha sits
at jyotisha › nakshatras › Magha. The path is a list of at most two
short names in the `group` field. `group_by` tells who set it: `hand`
for the learner, `model` for the tutor. The tutor never moves a concept
that the learner moved by hand. An old vault has no groups, so each
concept shows under “Not sorted yet”.

[`clean_group`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#clean_group)
makes a path safe to keep and to show. Each name has only letters,
digits, spaces and hyphens, and at most `GROUP_LEN` characters.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L675"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### clean_group

``` python
def clean_group(
    path, subject:str=''
)->list:
```

*`path` as at most `GROUP_DEPTH` short plain names. A text splits at
`/`, `>` or `›`. Empty parts, repeats and a first part that is the
subject drop.*

`set_group` moves one concept. A move by hand marks it. A move by the
model does not change a concept with the mark. An empty path by hand
also keeps the mark: the learner chose no group, so the tutor does not
sort the concept again. `groups` lists the paths in use under one
subject, with their parents, so a new concept can go in a group that is
there.

#### Sort by hand

You can sort the concepts yourself. `rename` gives a concept a new name
and marks it `named_by='hand'`, so a new extract never renames it. The
old name stays as an alias, so the find box still finds it.
`rename_group` gives a group a new name. Each concept in the group, or
in a group below it, gets the new name and `group_by='hand'`. A name
that is the name of a group beside it, in any case and without marks,
joins the two groups. `new_group` adds an empty group. `hand_groups`
lists the groups that you made or renamed. “Sort everything again” keeps
them. `snapshot` and `restore` are the Undo of one change by hand:
`snapshot` keeps the fields that a change by hand can touch, and
`restore` writes them back.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L849"


[`tree`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#tree) puts
concepts in a tree for the Concepts page: a node for each subject, then
its groups, then their groups. A node has its `name`, its `path` under
the subject, `n` (the concepts in it and below it), `kids` (its groups
by name) and `cs` (its own concepts). A concept with no group is in `cs`
of its subject. Two names that differ only in case are one group.

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L896"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
    concepts, groups:NoneType=None
)->list:
```

*The subject nodes of `concepts`, sorted by name, each with its groups
and the count of concepts below it. `groups` (`{subject: paths}`) adds
groups with no concept, under a subject that shows.*

### Attempts

Each answer is one attempt document. Thus search can find what the
learner said. The tutor can also find old questions and not ask them
again.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L916"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### attempt_text

``` python
def attempt_text(
    a
)->str:
```

*The searchable text of an attempt: the question, the answer, the
think-aloud and the feedback.*

`record` saves one attempt. The vault joins two sources with the same
text into one document. So `record` asks for a new document each time
(`force=True`): two attempts with the same words stay two records. Each
one has its own source, `learning://attempt/<id>`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L924"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Search and graph

`search` uses the hybrid search of the vault. Each hit has the kind,
title and meta of its document. The method stats, the marker of a
repair, a session with no answers and an open question stay out of it.
Two attempts with the same text show as one hit. `graph` gives the nodes
and links for the graph view.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1015"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Learning.graph

``` python
def graph(
    subject:str=None
)->dict:
```

*Nodes and links (prereq, related, gap) for a graph view. A link to a
slug that has no concept is dropped.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L993"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Learning.search

``` python
def search(
    q:str, kind:str=None, limit:int=10
)->fastcore.foundation.L:
```

*Hybrid search over the shelf. Each hit also has the `kind`, `title` and
`meta` of its document, so a page can show it* by kind. The method
stats, the marker of a repair, the history of the changes to a talk or a
walk, a session with no answers and an open question stay out: they have
no text that you wrote or learned, and an open question has its answer
key.

### A shelf for tests

Each test uses a vault in a temporary folder with the offline hashing
encoder. The tests never open the real vault of the learner.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1026"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### temp_learning

``` python
def temp_learning(
    **kw
)->__main__.Learning:
```

*A
[`Learning`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#learning)
on a new vault in a temporary folder (vishalakshi `Vault.temp`), with
the offline hashing encoder.*

### Tests

`put` makes a concept with the start state and the slug from its name.

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
c = lr.put('Reciprocal rank fusion', 'Merge ranked lists by summing 1/(k + rank) for each item.', 'ml', prereqs=['ranking'], aliases=['RRF'])
test_eq(c.slug, 'reciprocal-rank-fusion')
test_eq(c.floor, 0)
test_eq(c.prereqs, ['ranking'])
```

[`update`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#update)
changes the state.

``` python
c = lr.update(c.slug, floor=3, stability=2.)
test_eq((c.floor, c.stability), (3, 2.))
```

A concept keeps its `core` and its wrong ideas. A later `put` with no
`core` keeps them. A wrong idea as a plain string becomes a dict.

``` python
wl = temp_learning()
c = wl.put('Token embeddings', 'Each token ID picks a row of a learned matrix.', 'ml', core='Each token gets a learned vector, so tokens used in the same way end up close.',
           wrong=['the ID number itself carries meaning', dict(think='the vectors are fixed', fact='training changes them')])
test_eq(c.wrong, [dict(think='the ID number itself carries meaning', fact=''), dict(think='the vectors are fixed', fact='training changes them')])
test_eq(wl.put('Token embeddings', 'Rows of E.').core, c.core)
```

A second `put` keeps the learner state and merges the lists, also when
the text changes.

``` python
c = lr.put('Reciprocal rank fusion', 'Merge ranked lists: score is the sum of 1/(k + rank).', related=['bm25'], aliases=['RRF', 'rank fusion'])
test_eq(c.floor, 3)
test_eq(c.subject, 'ml')
test_eq(c.aliases, ['RRF', 'rank fusion'])
test_eq(c.related, ['bm25'])
test_eq(len(lr.concepts()), 1)
```

`concepts` and `subjects` filter by subject. `graph` keeps only the
links between known concepts.

``` python
lr.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
lr.put('Sandhi', 'Sounds change where words meet.', 'sanskrit')
test_eq(len(lr.concepts('ml')), 2)
test_eq({r['subject'] for r in lr.subjects()}, {'ml', 'sanskrit'})
g = lr.graph()
test_eq(g['links'], [dict(source='ranking', target='reciprocal-rank-fusion', kind='prereq')])
```

`record` saves an attempt. `attempts` and `search` find it again.

``` python
a = lr.record('reciprocal-rank-fusion', 'Why does RRF ignore raw scores?', answer='Because scores from different systems are not comparable.',
              thinking='bm25 and cosine have different scales', correct=True, confidence=80, depth=3)
test_eq(lr.attempts('reciprocal-rank-fusion')[0].id, a.id)
test_eq(lr.attempts('ranking'), [])
test(lr.search('scales comparable', kind='attempt'), [], lambda a,b: len(a) > 0)
```

`drop` removes a concept.

``` python
lr.drop('ranking')
test_is(lr.concept('ranking'), None)
```

#### Shelves of documents

A real vault also keeps a store of names, `entities`, with no `doc_id`
column. `shelf_names` leaves it out. It keeps the main shelf, the
learning shelf and a shelf of notebooks.

``` python
dv = temp_learning()
dv.vault.shelf('notebooks').add('Notes on softmax.', title='nbs/softmax', source='/x/softmax.md', kind='md')
dv.vault.db.get_graph('store', ann=False)   # the store of names, as vishalakshi makes it
assert 'entities' in dv.vault.db.table_names()   # the store of names is in the vault, though vishalakshi 0.1.36 no longer lists it as a shelf
test_eq(sorted(dv.vault.shelf_names()), ['learning', 'notebooks', 'store'])
```

`shelf_names` reads only the names of the stores. It does not count the
documents of each store, so SQLite logs no error for a store of names
with no `docs` table. A page can call it many times.

``` python
import logging
```

``` python
class _Seen(logging.Handler):
    def __init__(self): super().__init__(); self.got = []
    def emit(self, r): self.got.append(r.getMessage())
seen, root = _Seen(), logging.getLogger()
root.addHandler(seen)
try: test_eq(sorted(dv.vault.shelf_names()), ['learning', 'notebooks', 'store'])
finally: root.removeHandler(seen)
test_eq([m for m in seen.got if 'no such table' in m], [])
```

`doc_shelf` opens a shelf of documents. It gives None for the store of
names and for a name that is not in the vault, and it does not make that
shelf.

``` python
test_eq(dv.doc_shelf('notebooks').t.docs()[0]['title'], 'nbs/softmax')
test_is(dv.doc_shelf('store'), dv.vault)
test_is(dv.doc_shelf('entities'), None)
test_is(dv.doc_shelf('nope'), None)
assert 'nope' not in [s['store'] for s in dv.vault.shelves()]
```

The search fetches more hits until it has `limit` real hits, or the
shelf has no more. Here 30 sessions with no answers match the words
best. Three concepts match only one word. All three concepts come back.

``` python
sl = temp_learning()
for k in range(30): sl.log_session(f'empty{k}', f'zebra quagga okapi zebra quagga okapi {k}', start=1., log=[])
for k in range(3): sl.put(f'Giraffe {k}', f'A tall animal {k}, once next to an okapi.', 'zoo')
test_eq(len(sl.search('zebra quagga okapi', limit=3)), 3)
```

``` python
lr.log_session('s1', '1 of 2 passed.', start=1., updated=2., asked=2)
lr.log_session('s1', '1 of 2 passed.', start=1., updated=3., asked=2, ended=3.)   # the same text: the meta still changes
test_eq((lr.session('s1').updated, lr.session('s1').ended, lr.session('s1').summary), (3., 3., '1 of 2 passed.'))
test_eq(len(lr.sessions()), 1)
```

`sessions` lists the most recently changed session first.

``` python
lr.log_session('s2', 'Started.', start=5., updated=5.)
test_eq(lr.sessions().attrgot('id'), ['s2', 's1'])
test_is(lr.session('nope'), None)
```

With `journey`, `sessions` reads only the sessions of that walk, in the
store.

``` python
lr.log_session('s3', 'A walk.', start=6., journey='j1')
test_eq(lr.sessions(journey='j1').attrgot('id'), ['s3'])
test_eq(len(lr.sessions()), 3)
```

`search` leaves out a session with no answers and the method stats. The
session is still filed, so you can continue it. Each hit names its kind.

``` python
lr.log_session('s4', '0 of 0 passed. Concepts: none.', start=7., log=[])
lr.v.add('How you learn: method counts, passed.', title='How you learn', source='stats:test', kind='stats')
hs = lr.search('passed', limit=20)
test_eq([h for h in hs if h['kind'] == 'stats' or h['meta'].get('id') == 's4'], [])
test_eq('s1' in [h['meta'].get('id') for h in hs if h['kind'] == 'session'], True)   # a session with answers stays
test_eq(lr.session('s4').id, 's4')
```

The search fetches more hits until it has `limit` real hits, or the
shelf has no more. Here 30 sessions with no answers match the words
first, and three concepts match them too. All three concepts come back.

`concept_by_doc` gives the concept of a search hit. It gives None for a
hit that is not a concept.

``` python
cl = temp_learning()
cl.put('Reciprocal rank fusion', 'Merge ranked lists by summing 1/(k + rank).', 'ml')
cl.record('reciprocal-rank-fusion', 'Why ranks?', answer='scales differ')
test_eq(cl.concept_by_doc(cl.search('rank fusion', kind='concept')[0]['doc_id']).slug, 'reciprocal-rank-fusion')
test_is(cl.concept_by_doc(cl.search('scales differ', kind='attempt')[0]['doc_id']), None)
```

[`slugify`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#slugify)
reads Devanagari and Telugu, keeps C, C++ and C# apart, and gives the
same hash slug for the same unreadable name.

``` python
test_eq([slugify(s) for s in ('saṃdhi', 'संधि', 'గుణ', 'C', 'C++', 'C#', 'R&D')], ['samdhi', 'samdhi', 'guna', 'c', 'c-plus-plus', 'c-sharp', 'r-and-d'])
test_eq(slugify('学习'), slugify('学习'))
assert slugify('学习').startswith('c-')
```

This test makes a vault for `reslug` as abhyasa 0.0.5 left it: C# saved
as `c`, a Devanagari name with a random slug, and links, an attempt and
a session that use these slugs.

``` python
ol = temp_learning()
ol.put('C#', 'A language from Microsoft.', 'code', slug='c')
ol.put('संधि', 'Sounds change where words meet.', 'sanskrit', slug='a1b2c3d4')
ol.put('karaka term', 'A set slug.', 'sanskrit', slug='sa-term-karaka')
ol.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml', prereqs=['c'], related=['a1b2c3d4', 'sa-term-karaka'])
ol.record('c', 'What is C#?', answer='c')
ol.log_session('s1', 'One question.', concepts=['c'], log=[dict(concept='c', question='What is C#?')], focus='a1b2c3d4')
```

A dry run lists the moves and changes nothing. A slug that a source sets
is not in the list.

``` python
test_eq(ol.reslug(dry_run=True), {'c': 'c-sharp', 'a1b2c3d4': 'samdhi'})
assert ol.concept('c') is not None and ol.concept('c-sharp') is None
```

The real run moves the concepts and every slug that points to them. An
answer that is the text `c` stays as it is. A second run has nothing to
do.

``` python
test_eq(ol.reslug(), {'c': 'c-sharp', 'a1b2c3d4': 'samdhi'})
test_eq((ol.concept('c'), ol.concept('a1b2c3d4')), (None, None))
test_eq((ol.concept('c-sharp').name, ol.concept('samdhi').statement), ('C#', 'Sounds change where words meet.'))
r = ol.concept('ranking')
test_eq((r.prereqs, r.related), (['c-sharp'], ['samdhi', 'sa-term-karaka']))
a = ol.attempts('c-sharp')[0]
test_eq((a.concept, a.answer), ('c-sharp', 'c'))
s = ol.session('s1')
test_eq((s.concepts, s.log[0]['concept'], s.focus), (['c-sharp'], 'c-sharp', 'samdhi'))
test_eq(ol.reslug(), {})
```

`mark_attempt` changes a saved attempt. `add_gap` keeps each gap one
time, and `graph` shows it as a `gap` link.

``` python
gl = temp_learning()
gl.put('Functions and the neuron', 'z = w . x + b.', 'ml'); gl.put('Weighted sum', 'Add each input times its weight.', 'ml')
a = gl.record('functions-and-the-neuron', 'Why does z double?', answer='2z')
test_eq(gl.mark_attempt(a.id, taught=True)['taught'], True)
test_eq(gl.attempts('functions-and-the-neuron')[0].taught, True)
gl.add_gap('functions-and-the-neuron', 'weighted-sum'); gl.add_gap('functions-and-the-neuron', 'weighted-sum')
test_eq(gl.concept('functions-and-the-neuron').gaps, ['weighted-sum'])
assert dict(source='weighted-sum', target='functions-and-the-neuron', kind='gap') in gl.graph()['links']
```

Two attempts with the same text are two records. The vault does not join
them, so each one counts in your history and in the misses that the
tutor counts. A field added later goes on the right attempt.

``` python
ld = temp_learning(); ld.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
a1, a2 = [ld.record('ranking', 'What is a rank?', 'a score', feedback='Look at positions.', final=True) for _ in range(2)]
test_eq(ld.attempts('ranking').attrgot('id'), [a2.id, a1.id])
ld.mark_attempt(a2.id, taught=1)
test_eq([a.get('taught') for a in ld.attempts('ranking')], [1, None])
```

A search shows the same attempt text only once.

``` python
test_eq(len([h for h in ld.search('What is a rank', kind='attempt') if h['kind'] == 'attempt']), 1)
```

### Groups

An old vault has no groups. A concept loads with an empty path, and no
one set it.

``` python
gv = temp_learning()
m = gv.put('Magha', 'The tenth nakshatra.', 'jyotisha')
test_eq((m.get('group'), m.get('group_by')), (None, None))
```

[`clean_group`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#clean_group)
keeps at most two short plain names. It drops marks, empty parts, a
repeat and a first part that is the subject. A text splits at `/`, `>`
or `›`.

``` python
test_eq(clean_group(['Nakshatras', 'Padas', 'More']), ['Nakshatras', 'Padas'])
test_eq(clean_group(' nakshatras  /  padas! '), ['nakshatras', 'padas'])
test_eq(clean_group(['Nakshatras!', '  deva   gana? ']), ['Nakshatras', 'deva gana'])
test_eq(clean_group(['jyotisha', 'nakshatras'], 'jyotisha'), ['nakshatras'])
test_eq(clean_group(['', 'Nakshatras', 'nakshatras', 3]), ['Nakshatras'])
test_eq(clean_group('saṃdhi › स्वर'), ['saṃdhi', 'स्वर'])
test_eq(len(clean_group(['x' * 90])[0]), GROUP_LEN)
test_eq((clean_group(None), clean_group({'a': 1}), clean_group('')), ([], [], []))
```

`set_group` by the model moves a concept. A move by hand sets
`group_by='hand'`. After that, a move by the model changes nothing.

``` python
test_eq(gv.set_group('magha', ['nakshatras'], by='model').group, ['nakshatras'])
m = gv.set_group('magha', 'Nakshatras / Gana')
test_eq((m.group, m.group_by), (['Nakshatras', 'Gana'], 'hand'))
test_eq(gv.set_group('magha', ['rasis'], by='model').group, ['Nakshatras', 'Gana'])
```

A new `put` with a group, as from a new source, does not move a concept
that you moved by hand. It keeps the learner state.

``` python
m = gv.put('Magha', 'The tenth nakshatra, ruled by Ketu.', 'jyotisha', group=['rasis'], group_by='model')
test_eq((m.group, m.group_by, m.statement), (['Nakshatras', 'Gana'], 'hand', 'The tenth nakshatra, ruled by Ketu.'))
```

An empty path by hand takes the concept out of its group and keeps the
mark. So the tutor does not sort it again, and a move by the model
changes nothing.

``` python
m = gv.set_group('magha', '')
test_eq((m.group, m.group_by), ([], 'hand'))
test_eq(gv.set_group('magha', ['rasis'], by='model').group, [])
```

`groups` lists the paths in use under one subject, with their parents. A
path in another subject does not show.

`set_subject` gives a subject to a concept that has none. A move by the
tutor never changes a concept that you moved by hand, and it never
replaces a subject. A move by hand always works.

``` python
sj = temp_learning()
sj.put('Alpha', 'One.'); sj.put('Beta', 'Two.'); sj.put('Gamma', 'Three.', 'ml')
sj.set_group('beta', 'mine')
test_eq(sj.set_subject('alpha', ' Star  Maps! ').subject, 'star maps')
test_eq(sj.concept('alpha').subject_by, 'model')
test_eq(sj.set_subject('beta', 'stars').subject, '')                 # moved by hand: the tutor does not touch it
test_eq(sj.set_subject('gamma', 'stars').subject, 'ml')              # it has a subject
test_eq(sj.set_subject('gamma', 'stars', by='hand').subject, 'stars')
```

A name that is its own slug, with hyphens, gets a readable name one
time. A name that differs from the slug stays. The empty name of the
finder gets words from the statement.

``` python
test_eq(readable_name('attention-heads-and-anaphora-resolution'), 'Attention heads and anaphora resolution')
test_eq(readable_name('Softmax'), 'Softmax'); test_eq(readable_name('softmax'), 'softmax'); test_eq(readable_name('my-Note'), 'my-Note')
test_eq(readable_name('', 'A rank is a position in a list. More.'), 'A rank is a position in')
rn = temp_learning()
rn.put('attention-heads-and-anaphora-resolution', 'Heads.', 'ml', slug='attention-heads-and-anaphora-resolution')
rn.put('my-note', 'Mine.', 'ml', slug='note')
rn.put('foo-bar', 'Typed.', 'ml', slug='foo-bar', named_by='hand')
def old_vault(l):
    "Forget the mark of the repair, as in a vault from before it."
    l.v.forget(first(l.v.t.docs(where='source=?', where_args=['learning://marker/names']))['id'])
old_vault(rn)
test_eq(Learning(rn.vault).concept('attention-heads-and-anaphora-resolution').name, 'Attention heads and anaphora resolution')
test_eq((rn.concept('note').name, rn.concept('foo-bar').name), ('my-note', 'foo-bar'))   # a name that differs from the slug, or that you typed, stays
test_eq(rn.repair_names(), [])
```

The repair runs one time: a mark on the shelf says that it ran. A vault
that cannot be read or changed does not break the load. A change of name
or subject also makes the search text and the title again.

``` python
from unittest.mock import patch as mock_patch
```

``` python
rn.put('late-slug-name', 'Late.', 'ml', slug='late-slug-name')
test_eq(rn.repair_names(), [])                                        # the mark is set: it does not look again
test_eq(rn.concept('late-slug-name').name, 'late-slug-name')
old_vault(rn)
with mock_patch.object(Learning, 'repair_names', side_effect=OSError('read only')): Learning(rn.vault)   # the load goes on
test_eq(rn.repair_names(), ['late-slug-name'])
doc = lambda l, s: first(l.v.t.docs(where='source=?', where_args=[f'learning://concept/{s}']))
test_eq(doc(rn, 'late-slug-name')['title'], 'Late slug name')
sj.set_subject('gamma', 'cosmos', by='hand')
test_eq(sj.concept('gamma').subject, 'cosmos')
assert sj.concept('gamma').doc_id in [h['doc_id'] for h in sj.v.search('cosmos', 3)]   # the search text has the new subject
```

The mark of the repair is a document, but search never gives it.

``` python
mt = temp_learning(); mt.put('Names', 'Names of concepts repaired.', 'ml')
assert first(mt.v.t.docs(where='kind=?', where_args=['marker']))
test_eq([h['kind'] for h in mt.search('names concepts repaired')], ['concept'])
test_eq(mt.search('Names repaired', kind='marker'), [])
```

#### Saved groups stay

When you save a sort, the tutor keeps the group list of each subject and
does not move a sorted concept again. `save_groups` keeps the list.
`groups` gives the saved groups and the groups in use. A saved group
stays when no concept is in it. `unsorted` lists the concepts that the
tutor may still place: no group, and not set by hand.

``` python
cl = temp_learning()
for n in ('Ashvini', 'Bharani', 'Krittika'): cl.put(n, f'{n}.', 'jyotisha')
test_is(cl.saved_groups('jyotisha'), None)
cl.set_group('ashvini', ['Stars'], by='sort')
test_eq(cl.save_groups('jyotisha'), [['Stars']])
cl.set_group('ashvini', [], by='hand'); cl.set_group('bharani', ['Signs'], by='sort')
test_eq(cl.save_groups('jyotisha'), [['Signs'], ['Stars']])           # a kept group stays when no concept is in it
test_eq(cl.groups('jyotisha'), [['Signs'], ['Stars']])
test_eq(cl.saved_groups('JYOTISHA'), [['Signs'], ['Stars']])
test_eq(cl.concept('bharani').group_by, 'sort')
```

A concept with a group is sorted. A concept with no group is not sorted,
except when you set it by hand to no group. `unplace` is the Undo of a
placement by the tutor: the concept has no group, and the tutor does not
place it by itself again.

``` python
test_eq(cl.unsorted('jyotisha').attrgot('slug'), ['krittika'])         # ashvini: kept out by hand; bharani: sorted
cl.set_group('krittika', ['Stars'], by='placed')
test_eq(cl.unplace('krittika').group_by, 'undone')
test_eq((cl.concept('krittika').group, cl.unsorted('jyotisha').attrgot('slug')), ([], ['krittika']))
test_eq(cl.unplace('bharani').group, ['Signs'])                         # only a placement by the tutor can be undone
test_eq(cl.unplace('ashvini').group_by, 'hand')
```

A name with fewer than two characters, or with no letter or digit, is
not an idea:
[`usable_name`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#usable_name)
says so,
[`idea_name`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#idea_name)
is the rule for the name of a new concept: a letter or a digit, and not
one small letter such as `x`. One capital letter, such as `C`, is a
name. `put` refuses a new concept with another name, so no tool, plan or
text can file one. A plan or a gap has no source text, so it also needs
[`real_idea`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#real_idea):
a statement of 3 words or more. Library and the graph leave out a
concept that breaks the name rule or has a statement of one word
([`listed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#listed)),
such as the `x` that an older tool filed. The marker and the group list
never show in search.

``` python
assert usable_name('Ab') and usable_name('x2') and usable_name('C#') and not usable_name('x') and not usable_name(' - ') and not usable_name(None)
test_fail(lambda: cl.put('x', 'x', 'code'), contains='not the name of an idea')         # one small letter
test_fail(lambda: cl.put('z', 'z is a letter for a value.', 'code'), contains='not the name of an idea')
test_eq(cl.put('C', 'C is a compiled systems language.', 'code').name, 'C')            # one capital letter
assert cl.concept('x') is None and listed(cl.concept('c')) and not listed(dict(name='Bias', statement='x'))
test_eq((real_idea('Bias', 'x'), real_idea('C', 'C is a language.')), (False, True))   # with no source text, a statement of 3 words or more
cl.drop('c')
test_eq(cl.search('Groups of jyotisha', kind='groups'), [])
assert not [h for h in cl.search('Groups of jyotisha') if h['kind'] == 'groups']
```

``` python
gv.put('Ashvini', 'The first nakshatra.', 'jyotisha', group=['nakshatras', 'deva gana'])
gv.put('Mesha', 'The first rasi.', 'jyotisha', group=['Rasis'])
gv.put('Sandhi', 'Sounds change where words meet.', 'sanskrit', group=['phonology'])
test_eq(gv.groups('jyotisha'), [['nakshatras'], ['nakshatras', 'deva gana'], ['Rasis']])
test_eq(gv.groups('ml'), [])
```

[`tree`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#tree) puts
the concepts under their subject, then their groups. Each node has the
count of the concepts in it and below it. A concept with no group is an
item of its subject. A group name in another case is the same group.

``` python
gv.put('Bharani', 'The second nakshatra.', 'jyotisha', group=['Nakshatras'])
t = tree(gv.concepts())
test_eq([(s.name, s.n) for s in t], [('jyotisha', 4), ('sanskrit', 1)])
j = t[0]
test_eq([(k.name, k.n) for k in j.kids], [('nakshatras', 2), ('Rasis', 1)])
test_eq([c.name for c in j.cs], ['Magha'])
test_eq([(k.path, [c.name for c in k.cs]) for k in j.kids[0].kids], [(['nakshatras', 'deva gana'], ['Ashvini'])])
test_eq([c.name for c in j.kids[0].cs], ['Bharani'])
```

#### Sort by hand

A renamed group takes its concepts with it. They and the group get the
hand mark, so the tutor never moves them.

``` python
hs = temp_learning()
for n in ('Ashvini', 'Bharani'): hs.put(n, f'{n}.', 'jyotisha', group=['nakshatras'])
hs.save_groups('jyotisha')
test_eq(sorted(hs.rename_group('jyotisha', ['Nakshatras'], 'Lunar mansions')), ['ashvini', 'bharani'])
test_eq({(tuple(c.group), c.group_by) for c in hs.concepts('jyotisha')}, {(('Lunar mansions',), 'hand')})
test_eq((hs.hand_groups('jyotisha'), hs.groups('jyotisha')), ([['Lunar mansions']], [['Lunar mansions']]))
assert not hs.unsorted('jyotisha') and not hs.place('ashvini', ['Other'])
```

A name that is the name of a group beside it, in another case, joins the
two groups. The group below a renamed group moves with it.

``` python
hs.put('Pada', 'A quarter.', 'jyotisha', group=['Stars', 'padas']); hs.put('Pada two', 'A quarter.', 'jyotisha', group=['Stars x'])
hs.rename_group('jyotisha', ['Stars x'], 'STARS')
test_eq(hs.concept('pada-two').group, ['Stars'])
hs.rename_group('jyotisha', ['Stars'], 'Asterisms')
test_eq((hs.concept('pada').group, hs.concept('pada-two').group), (['Asterisms', 'padas'], ['Asterisms']))
assert ['Stars'] not in hs.groups('jyotisha') and ['Stars x'] not in hs.groups('jyotisha')
test_fail(lambda: hs.rename_group('jyotisha', ['Asterisms'], '!!!'), contains='letters or digits')
```

`new_group` adds an empty group that stays. `save_groups(replace=True)`
makes the list again and keeps the hand groups. `unmark_groups` takes
the mark off.

``` python
hs.new_group('jyotisha', 'Rasis')
assert ['Rasis'] in hs.groups('jyotisha') and ['Rasis'] in hs.hand_groups('jyotisha')
test_eq(hs.save_groups('jyotisha', [['Grahas']], replace=True), [['Asterisms'], ['Grahas'], ['Lunar mansions'], ['Rasis']])
assert ['Asterisms', 'padas'] in hs.groups('jyotisha')   # a group in use still shows
hs.unmark_groups('jyotisha', [['rasis']])
assert ['Rasis'] not in hs.hand_groups('jyotisha') and ['Rasis'] in hs.groups('jyotisha')
```

A name that you set stays when a new extract puts the concept again. The
old name becomes an alias.

``` python
hs.put('Self-attention', 'x', 'ml'); c = hs.rename('self-attention', 'Attention over one sequence')
test_eq((c.name, c.named_by, c.aliases), ('Attention over one sequence', 'hand', ['Self-attention']))
test_eq(hs.put('Self-attention', 'y', 'ml').name, 'Attention over one sequence')
test_fail(lambda: hs.rename('self-attention', ' x '), contains='two letters')
test_eq(hs.rename('self-attention', 'Self\x00 at\x1b[31mtention\n' + 'x' * 200).name, 'Self at [31mtention ' + 'x' * 100)   # no control characters, and a cap
hs.rename('self-attention', 'Attention over one sequence')
test_eq(hs.put('Bad\x07 name', 'x', 'ml').name, 'Bad name')
```

`snapshot` and `restore` undo one change by hand: the groups of the
concepts, their names and the group list.

``` python
snap = hs.snapshot(['pada', 'self-attention'], ['jyotisha'])
hs.rename_group('jyotisha', ['Asterisms'], 'Stars again'); hs.rename('self-attention', 'Self focus'); hs.new_group('jyotisha', 'Extra')
test_eq(sorted(hs.restore(snap)), ['pada', 'self-attention'])
test_eq((hs.concept('pada').group, hs.concept('self-attention').name), (['Asterisms', 'padas'], 'Attention over one sequence'))
assert ['Extra'] not in hs.groups('jyotisha') and ['Asterisms'] in hs.saved_groups('jyotisha')
snap = hs.snapshot([], ['ml']); test_is(hs.saved_groups('ml'), None)
hs.new_group('ml', 'Heads'); hs.restore(snap)
test_is(hs.saved_groups('ml'), None)   # Undo takes away a list that was not there
```

## The learner model

The learner model: how deep you know each concept, when to review it,
and what to ask next.

This module holds the learner model as plain functions with no model
calls and no storage. It finds what an answer means, updates the state
of a concept, finds the next depth and picks the next concept. The tutor
calls these functions and the store keeps their results.

Import the tools that this module uses.

### Depth

Each concept has a depth from 0 to 5. The tutor asks each question at
one depth.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
<col style="width: 33%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>depth</th>
<th>name</th>
<th>a question at this depth asks you to</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>0</td>
<td><code>unseen</code></td>
<td>(no question)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>1</td>
<td><code>recognise</code></td>
<td>pick the correct statement from options</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>2</td>
<td><a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#recall"><code>recall</code></a></td>
<td>state the idea or the rule</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>3</td>
<td><a
href="https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#explain"><code>explain</code></a></td>
<td>say why it is true, in your own words</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>4</td>
<td><code>apply</code></td>
<td>use it to solve a problem</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>5</td>
<td><code>transfer</code></td>
<td>use it in a new case or link it to another subject</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

The floor is the highest depth that you pass reliably. The ceiling is
the lowest depth that you failed (6 until you fail). The next question
goes between them. Thus each answer moves one edge of this range.

These constants name the depths, give the question kind at each depth,
and set the goal and the high-confidence line.

### Outcome

Correctness and confidence together tell what an answer means.

<table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th></th>
<th>high confidence</th>
<th>low confidence</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td>correct</td>
<td><code>solid</code></td>
<td><code>fragile</code></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>wrong</td>
<td><code>misconception</code></td>
<td><code>gap</code></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

“I don’t know” is a `gap`. A correct answer that used two or more hints
is `fragile`.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1036"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### outcome

``` python
def outcome(
    correct:bool, confidence:int=None, hints:int=0, dont_know:bool=False
)->str:
```

*One of `solid`, `fragile`, `misconception` or `gap`. With no
`confidence`, only the answer and the hints count.*

A correct answer is `solid` with high confidence. Two hints or low
confidence make it `fragile`.

``` python
test_eq(outcome(True, 80), 'solid')
test_eq(outcome(True, 80, hints=2), 'fragile')
test_eq(outcome(True, 30), 'fragile')
```

With no confidence given, a clean pass is `solid` and a wrong answer is
a `gap`, never a `misconception`.

``` python
test_eq([outcome(True), outcome(True, hints=2), outcome(False)], ['solid', 'fragile', 'gap'])
```

A wrong answer is a `misconception` with high confidence, else a `gap`.
“I don’t know” is always a `gap`.

``` python
test_eq(outcome(False, 90), 'misconception')
test_eq(outcome(False, 20), 'gap')
test_eq(outcome(True, 90, dont_know=True), 'gap')
```

### Memory

Recall falls with time as in FSRS:
$R(t) = (1 + \frac{19}{81}\frac{t}{S})^{-1/2}$. The time *t* and the
stability *S* are in days. At *t* = *S*, recall is 90%. Thus the due
date is the last review plus *S* days.

[`recall`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#recall)
gives the recall now.
[`grow`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#grow) gives
the new stability after an outcome.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1050"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### grow

``` python
def grow(
    s:float, r:float, kind:str
)->float:
```

*The new stability after an outcome, from the old stability `s` and the
recall `r` at the time of the answer.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1044"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### recall

``` python
def recall(
    c, now:float=None
)->float:
```

*The chance, from 0 to 1, that you still recall concept `c` now.*

Recall is 90% after *S* days, and 0 for a concept with no review.

``` python
test_close(recall(dict(stability=2., last=0.), now=2*DAY), .9, eps=1e-6)
test_eq(recall(dict(stability=0, last=None)), 0.)
```

A pass grows stability. A harder recall grows it more. A gap shrinks it.

``` python
test_eq(grow(0, 0, 'solid'), 1.)
assert grow(4, .7, 'solid') > grow(4, .99, 'solid') > 4   # a review that was harder to recall teaches more
assert grow(4, .9, 'gap') < 4
```

### Update

[`update`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#update)
returns the fields to change after one answer at depth `d`.

<table>
<colgroup>
<col style="width: 50%" />
<col style="width: 50%" />
</colgroup>
<thead>
<tr>
<th>outcome</th>
<th>change</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td><code>solid</code></td>
<td>The floor rises to <code>d</code>. The streak grows.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>fragile</code></td>
<td>The floor stays. The concept is <code>shaky</code> at
<code>d</code>, so the next question is at <code>d</code> again.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>misconception</code></td>
<td>The ceiling falls to <code>d</code>. The floor falls below
<code>d</code>. The misconception is kept.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td><code>gap</code></td>
<td>The ceiling falls to <code>d</code>. The floor falls below
<code>d</code>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1058"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### update

``` python
def update(
    c, depth:int, correct:bool, confidence:int=None, hints:int=0, dont_know:bool=False, misconception:str='',
    now:float=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*The state changes for concept `c` after one answer at `depth`, with the
outcome in `kind`.*

A `solid` pass at depth 3 on a new concept raises the floor to 3. The
review is due in one day (the setting `review.solid`).

``` python
c = AttrDict(floor=0, ceiling=6, stability=0., last=None, streak=0, misses=0, seen=0)
u = update(c, 3, True, 80, now=0.)
test_eq((u.kind, u.floor, u.ceiling, u.streak, u.due), ('solid', 3, 6, 1, DAY))
c.update(u)
```

A confident wrong answer at depth 4 lowers the ceiling to 4 and keeps
the misconception.

``` python
u = update(c, 4, False, 85, misconception='thinks RRF needs normalised scores', now=DAY)
test_eq((u.kind, u.floor, u.ceiling, u.misses), ('misconception', 3, 4, 1))
test_eq(u.misconceptions, ['thinks RRF needs normalised scores'])
c.update(u)
```

A miss below the floor lowers the floor. A low-confidence pass makes the
concept `shaky` at that depth.

``` python
u = update(c, 2, False, 10, now=DAY)    # a miss below the floor: the floor falls
test_eq((u.kind, u.floor, u.ceiling), ('gap', 1, 2))
test_eq(update(c, 4, True, 30).shaky, 4)
```

### The next depth

Ask in the middle of the range between floor and ceiling, so one answer
cuts the range in half. Ask a `shaky` concept at the same depth again.
When the ceiling is the floor plus 1, ask at the ceiling, because the
work is at that edge.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1076"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### next_depth

``` python
def next_depth(
    c
)->int:
```

*The depth for the next question on concept `c`.*

A new concept starts at depth 3 (explain). An open range gives its
middle.

``` python
test_eq(next_depth(dict(floor=0, ceiling=6)), 3)     # a new concept: start at explain, not at the bottom
test_eq(next_depth(dict(floor=3, ceiling=6)), 4)
test_eq(next_depth(dict(floor=0, ceiling=3)), 1)
test_eq(next_depth(dict(floor=1, ceiling=3)), 2)
```

A closed range gives the ceiling. Depth 5 is the top. A `shaky` depth
comes first.

``` python
test_eq(next_depth(dict(floor=2, ceiling=3)), 3)
test_eq(next_depth(dict(floor=5, ceiling=6)), 5)
test_eq(next_depth(dict(floor=1, ceiling=6, shaky=4)), 4)
```

### What to ask next

[`pick`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#pick)
chooses the concept. Code makes the choice, not the model, so the app
can show the reason.

1.  A `focus` concept, when you chose one and did not learn it yet.
2.  A review that is due, with the lowest recall first.
3.  The frontier: concepts below the goal with all prereqs at depth 3 or
    more. Concepts that you started come first.

After two misses in a row on a concept,
[`pick`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#pick) goes
back to its weakest prereq that is below the goal.

[`learned`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#learned)
and [`ready`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#ready)
test one concept.
[`_back`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#_back)
finds the prereq to go back to. After a demo, it waits for the demo
ladder (see below).

### Strengths and weak spots

[`understanding`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#understanding)
reads one concept and tells how well you know it: the floor, the
ceiling, the recall now, and the reasons that it is weak. It uses only
the state of the concept. Thus a page of all concepts does not need to
read the attempts.
[`weak`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#weak) is
true when a reason says that you need help now. `strong` needs depth 3
or more, recall of 80% or more, and no reasons.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1148"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### weak

``` python
def weak(
    c, now:float=None
)->bool:
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1132"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### understanding

``` python
def understanding(
    c, now:float=None
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*How well you know concept `c`: floor, ceiling, recall, the reasons it
is weak,
[`weak`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#weak),
`strong`, one `state`, and a score to sort by.*

A concept with a misconception and two misses is weak, with both
reasons. A deep, fresh concept with no misses is strong.

``` python
now = 1e6
u = understanding(dict(slug='a', floor=1, ceiling=3, misses=2, misconceptions=['scores add'], seen=3, stability=5., last=now), now)
test_eq((u.weak, u.strong, u.reasons[:2]), (True, False, ['a misconception: scores add', 'missed the last 2 times']))
s = understanding(dict(slug='b', floor=4, ceiling=6, seen=5, stability=30., last=now - DAY), now)
test_eq((s.weak, s.strong, s.reasons), (False, True, []))
test_eq(understanding(dict(slug='g', floor=0, provenance=[dict(src='gap')]), now).reasons, ['you said you did not know it'])
assert understanding(dict(slug='f', floor=3, seen=4, stability=1., last=now - 30 * DAY), now).reasons[0].startswith('recall is down to')
test_eq([u.state, s.state, understanding(dict(slug='n')).state], ['weak', 'strong', 'unseen'])
```

Three concepts: `b` needs `a`. The first pick is `a`, because `b` waits
for its prereq.

``` python
def C(slug, **kw): return AttrDict(slug=slug, name=slug, **{**dict(floor=0, ceiling=6, seen=0, misses=0, prereqs=[]), **kw})
cs = [C('a', order=0), C('b', prereqs=['a'], order=1), C('c', order=2)]
test_eq(pick(cs)[0].slug, 'a')                          # b waits for a
```

A started concept below the goal comes first. When `a` is learned, `b`
is ready.

``` python
cs[0].update(floor=3, seen=1, due=10*DAY, stability=10., last=0.)
test_eq(pick(cs, now=DAY)[0].slug, 'a')                 # a was started and is below the goal
cs[0].update(floor=4)
test_eq(pick(cs, now=DAY)[0].slug, 'b')                 # a is learned; b is ready
```

A due review comes before the frontier, at the floor of the concept.

``` python
r = pick(cs, now=11*DAY)
test_eq((r[0].slug, r[1]), ('a', 4))                    # a is due: a review at its floor
assert 'due for review' in r[2]
# a due concept with two misses goes back to its prereq; the why still says that it is a review, so the daily review limit counts it
r = pick([dict(slug='p', name='P', prereqs=[], floor=0), dict(slug='q', name='Q', prereqs=['p'], floor=2, seen=3, due=1., misses=2)], now=5*DAY)
test_eq(r[0]['slug'], 'p')
assert r[2].startswith('due for review: two misses on Q')
```

Two misses go back to the weakest prereq. A learned concept that is not
due gives no question.

``` python
cs[1].update(misses=2, seen=2, floor=1, ceiling=2); cs[0].update(floor=3, due=None)
test_eq(pick(cs, focus='b', now=DAY)[0].slug, 'a')      # two misses on b: step back to a
test_eq(pick([C('x', floor=4, seen=1, due=1e12)]), None)
```

After you saw a demo of a concept, `after_demo` on the concept counts
your misses since then (the demo module keeps it). While the demo ladder
runs,
[`_back`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#_back)
waits: it steps back only after the third miss since the demo. Here, `b`
has 4 misses in all.

The tests below need
[`set_val`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#set_val).

``` python
by = {c['slug']: c for c in cs}
test_eq([_back({**cs[1], 'misses': 4, 'after_demo': n}, by, 4)[0]['slug'] for n in (0, 1, 2, 3)], ['b', 'b', 'b', 'a'])
assert 'after its demo' in _back({**cs[1], 'misses': 4, 'after_demo': 3}, by, 4)[1]
```

With no demo in play, or with the setting `checks.demo_ladder` off, two
misses step back, as before.

``` python
test_eq(_back({**cs[1], 'misses': 2, 'after_demo': None}, by, 4)[0]['slug'], 'a')
set_val('checks.demo_ladder', False)
try: test_eq(_back({**cs[1], 'misses': 2, 'after_demo': 1}, by, 4)[0]['slug'], 'a')
finally: set_val('checks.demo_ladder', True)
```

A concept in `near` comes first on the frontier, before a concept you
started elsewhere.

``` python
cs = [C('far', order=0, seen=1), C('next', order=5)]
test_eq(pick(cs)[0].slug, 'far')
r = pick(cs, near={'next'})
test_eq(r[0].slug, 'next')
assert 'next to the concept you chose' in r[2]
```

A gap that you named on a concept comes first, at the easiest depth.
After you pass it, or after two questions on it, the concept comes back.

``` python
nn = dict(slug='neuron', name='Neuron', floor=0, ceiling=6, gaps=['wsum'])
ws = dict(slug='wsum', name='Weighted sum', floor=0, ceiling=6, seen=0)
c, d, why = pick([nn, ws], focus='neuron')
test_eq((c['slug'], d), ('wsum', 1)); assert 'you said you did not know Weighted sum' in why
test_eq(pick([nn, dict(ws, floor=1, seen=1)], focus='neuron')[0]['slug'], 'neuron')
test_eq(pick([nn, dict(ws, seen=2)], focus='neuron')[0]['slug'], 'neuron')
```

## Ways to learn

The ways you learn: six text ways (code, maths, analogies, worked
examples, diagrams and plain words), and demos, ordering, playgrounds,
boards and timelines. This module finds which ways work for you, and
when to try a new one.

Each question, hint and lesson uses one way to teach: its `method`. The
tutor picks the method before it writes the prompt. So the tag is known,
not guessed. When a question closes, its outcome counts for its method:
solid 1, shaky 0.5, a miss 0.

The counts give each method a Beta posterior, for each subject and over
all subjects.
[`choose`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#choose)
uses them in two ways:

- Drill: a weak concept gets your best method.
- Explore: a concept that is not weak sometimes gets another method. You
  set the chance (`explore` in the profile). First
  [`choose`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#choose)
  tries a method that got better recently. Else it uses a random draw (a
  Thompson sample).

The counts are in one `stats` document on the shelf. This document is
only a cache: `method_stats` builds it again from the attempts.

### The methods

`METHODS` maps each method to the line that the prompt gets.
`EXAMPLES_TO` maps the profile’s “examples that help” to methods, to set
the prior.

The text of the methods is one prompt, `ways`, that you can change in
Settings (see `prompts`). It has one section for each method.
[`way`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#way) gives
the text in use: its section of your saved text, else the line in
`METHODS`.

### join_ways

``` python
def join_ways(
    d:dict
)->str:
```

*The text of the prompt `ways` from a dict of way -\> text: a section
`[way]` for each method.*

With no saved text,
[`way`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#way) gives
the line in `METHODS`.

``` python
test_eq([way(m) for m in METHODS], list(METHODS.values()))
test_eq(way('nope'), '')
test_eq((prompt('ways'), [n for n in PROMPTS if n.startswith('way.')]), (WAYS, []))
ways_of(WAYS)['maths']
```

The prompt `ways` is one text with a section for each way. A line such
as `[code]` on its own starts the section of `code`, and the section
runs to the next such line.
[`ways_of`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#ways_of)
reads the sections and
[`join_ways`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#join_ways)
writes them. A saved text changes only the sections that it changes;
[`way`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#way) gives
the section of the way that it is asked for.

``` python
assert ways_of(join_ways(METHODS)) == METHODS
set_prompt('ways', join_ways({**METHODS, 'code': 'Use one short line of code.'}))
test_eq((way('code'), way('maths')), ('Use one short line of code.', METHODS['maths']))
ways_of(prompt('ways'))['code']
```

A text that drops, repeats, renames or empties a section, or that has
words before the first section, is refused with a plain message that
names the section. The saved text stays.

``` python
test_fail(lambda: set_prompt('ways', WAYS.split('[board]')[0]), contains='[board] is missing')
test_fail(lambda: set_prompt('ways', WAYS.replace('[board]', '[bored]')), contains='[bored] is not a way')
test_fail(lambda: set_prompt('ways', WAYS + '\n[code]\nTwice.'), contains='[code] is there more than once')
test_fail(lambda: set_prompt('ways', WAYS.replace(METHODS['maths'], '')), contains='[maths] has no text')
test_fail(lambda: set_prompt('ways', 'Use words.\n' + WAYS), contains='before the first section')
test_eq(way('code'), 'Use one short line of code.')
```

A text that a person saved for `way.maths` before `ways` existed is not
lost. The first read moves each saved `way.X` into the section `X` of
`ways`, with the default text in the other sections, and drops the old
names. A prompt that no code reads any more (`RETIRED`) is dropped the
same way. The file keeps the old names until the next save, and that
save writes the new ones.

``` python
register('kept', 'Kept', 'A prompt that the move does not touch.', 'Say hello.')
_path().write_text(json.dumps(dict(prompts={'way.maths': 'Use only one equation.', 'way.demo': 'Show one slider.', 'research.gather': 'Old.', 'kept': 'Hi.'})))
test_eq((way('maths'), way('demo'), way('code')), ('Use only one equation.', 'Show one slider.', METHODS['code']))
test_eq(sorted(saved()), ['kept', 'ways'])
set_prompt('kept', 'Say hi.')
test_eq(sorted(json.loads(_path().read_text())['prompts']), ['kept', 'ways'])
for n in ('ways', 'kept'): set_prompt(n, '')
del PROMPTS['kept']
test_eq(settings()['prompts'], {})
```

`stats` reads the stats document. It gives empty counts when there is no
document. `set_stats` writes the document. A lock makes sure that two
closes at the same time do not lose a count.

### Credit

[`credit`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#credit)
adds one outcome to the counts and returns the new stats. It keeps the
last 8 credits of each method, to find a method that gets better.

### Learning.credit_method

``` python
def credit_method(
    method:str, subject:str, kind:str, w:float=1.0

```

*Count outcome `kind` for `method` with the weight `w` in the stats
document.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1226"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### credit

``` python
def credit(
    st, method:str, subject:str, kind:str, w:float=1.0
)->dict:
```

*The stats `st` with one outcome `kind` added for `method` with the
weight `w`, in `subject` and in `*`. Only a full outcome (`w=1`) goes in
the recent credits.*

Solid adds 1 to `a`. A miss adds 1 to `b`. Shaky adds half to each. An
unknown outcome or method changes nothing.

``` python
st = credit(credit(credit(EMPTY, 'code', 'ml', 'solid'), 'code', 'ml', 'fragile'), 'maths', 'ml', 'gap')
test_eq(st['methods']['ml'], {'code': [1.5, .5], 'maths': [0., 1.]})
test_eq(st['methods']['*'], st['methods']['ml'])
test_eq(st['recent'], {'code': [1., .5], 'maths': [0.]})
test_eq(credit(st, 'code', 'ml', 'closed'), st)
```

#### Feedback counts a little

The row under a demo or a lesson also counts for the way of that demo or
lesson, with a small weight from `FEEDBACK`. “Not clear” adds 0.25 of a
miss, so four of them count as one miss, and one click does not decide
the way. “Just right” adds 0.1 of a pass. “Too simple” adds nothing: the
way worked, but the step was too small. A part of an outcome does not go
in the recent credits, so it does not make a way look better lately.

``` python
st = credit(EMPTY, 'analogy', 'ml', *FEEDBACK['unclear'])
test_eq(st['methods']['ml']['analogy'], [0., .25])
test_eq(st['recent'], {})
test_eq(credit(st, 'analogy', 'ml', *FEEDBACK['right'])['methods']['ml']['analogy'], [.1, .25])
```

### The posterior

[`posterior`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#posterior)
gives `(a, b)` for a method: Beta(1, 1), plus 2 on `a` for a method in
the profile’s examples. For a subject, it adds the subject counts and
the `*` counts. It scales the `*` counts down to at most 4
pseudo-counts. So a new subject starts from what works for you in other
subjects.

href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1255"
