With no counts, the prior decides.
[`improving`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#improving)
finds a method that got better recently.

``` python
test_eq(posterior(EMPTY, 'code'), (1., 1.))
test_eq(posterior(EMPTY, 'code', prior=['code']), (3., 1.))
gm = dict(methods={'*': {'maths': [2., 4.]}}, recent={'maths': [0., 0., 1., 1., 1., 1.]})
test_eq(improving(gm, 'maths'), (4, 5))
test_is(improving(dict(gm, recent={'maths': [1., 0., 0., 0.]}), 'maths'), None)
```

### Choose a method

[`choose`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#choose)
returns `(method, note)`. The note goes in the line that says why you
get this question.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1269"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### choose

``` python
def choose(
    st, subject:str='', weak:bool=False, rng:NoneType=None, explore:str='sometimes', prior:tuple=(),
    allowed:NoneType=None
)->tuple:
```

*The method for the next question, and a note on why, from the `allowed`
ways (default `TEXT_WAYS`). A weak concept gets the best method; else,
sometimes, another one.*

A weak concept gets the best method. With `explore='never'`,
[`choose`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#choose)
always gives the best method. With `sometimes`, it tries a method that
got better at times. It still gives the best method most of the time.

``` python
cs = dict(methods={'*': {'code': [7., 2.], 'maths': [2., 4.]}}, recent={'maths': [0., 0., 1., 1., 1., 1.]})
m, note = choose(cs, 'ml', weak=True)
test_eq(m, 'code'); assert note.startswith('drill with code: 7 of 9')
test_eq({choose(cs, 'ml', rng=random.Random(i), explore='never')[0] for i in range(30)}, {'code'})
picks = [choose(cs, 'ml', rng=random.Random(i)) for i in range(60)]
assert any(n.startswith('trying maths: you got better') for _, n in picks)
test_eq(sum(m == 'code' for m, _ in picks) > 30, True)   # with `sometimes`, the best method still comes most of the time
```

### The ways that fit

A session cannot show every way.
[`choose`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#choose)
takes `allowed`: the ways it may pick from. The default is `TEXT_WAYS`,
the ways that every session can show. A list with no known way gives
`TEXT_WAYS` too.

``` python
rng = random.Random(0)
assert {'demo', 'order', 'playground', 'board', 'timeline'} <= set(METHODS) and 'ways' in PROMPTS
assert all(choose(EMPTY, rng=rng)[0] in TEXT_WAYS for _ in range(200))          # a session never gets a way it cannot show
assert all(choose(EMPTY, rng=rng, allowed=['demo', 'maths'])[0] in ('demo', 'maths') for _ in range(200))
assert choose(EMPTY, rng=rng, allowed=['board'])[0] in METHODS                   # an allowed list keeps its own ways
assert choose(EMPTY, rng=rng, allowed=['nope'])[0] in TEXT_WAYS                  # no known way: back to the text ways
```

### The way for a check

[`check_for`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#check_for)
picks the way for one check of one idea. It looks only at the ways of
the idea that a walk can show. It does not repeat the way of the last
check when it has another. The kind of the check follows the way, and
the depth follows the kind. A short check is depth 3 or more: it asks
for the idea and why it holds, never for a fact to recall. It is depth 4
when the floor is 3 or more.

A hands-on way of the idea (a key of `CHECK_KIND`: demo, order or code)
comes before its text ways. The model lists a hands-on way only for an
idea that fits it: a process, a sequence, or code. A code check is a
notebook that runs in Leela. Without this rule, the learner stats and
the profile pick a text way almost every time, because the profile names
only text ways. Then nearly every check is a short answer.

Only the idea’s own ways can give a hands-on check. An idea with no way
that a walk can show gets a short answer in a text way. A walk passes
`hands=False` when it has its share of hands-on checks (see
[`hands_most`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/path.html#hands_most)
in `journey`).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1291"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### check_for

``` python
def check_for(
    c, st, rng:NoneType=None, explore:str='sometimes', prior:tuple=(), last:str='', hands:bool=True
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*The way, kind, depth and reason for one check of concept `c`. A
hands-on way of the idea comes before its text ways; `hands=False`
leaves the hands-on ways out.*

A check takes a way of its idea. An idea with no way that a walk can
show gets a text way.

``` python
c = AttrDict(ways=['code', 'maths'], floor=0)
k = check_for(c, EMPTY, rng=random.Random(1))
assert (k.way, k.kind, k.depth) in {('code', 'notebook', 4), ('maths', 'short', 3)} and k.why
assert check_for(AttrDict(ways=['demo'], floor=0), EMPTY).kind == 'demo'
assert check_for(AttrDict(ways=['timeline'], floor=3), EMPTY).way in TEXT_WAYS   # no timeline view yet
assert check_for(AttrDict(ways=['words'], floor=0), EMPTY).depth == 3   # a new idea: say the idea and why, not a fact
assert check_for(AttrDict(ways=['words'], floor=3), EMPTY).depth == 4
assert all(check_for(AttrDict(ways=['demo', 'code'], floor=0), EMPTY, rng=rng, last='demo').way == 'code' for _ in range(20))
```

An idea that lists a hands-on way (demo, order or code) gets a check of
that kind. This is true when a text way comes first in the list, and
when the profile likes a text way. An idea with only text ways still
gets a short answer.

``` python
assert all(check_for(AttrDict(ways=['words', 'example', 'order'], floor=0), EMPTY, random.Random(k), prior=['example']).kind == 'order' for k in range(50))
assert all(check_for(AttrDict(ways=['maths', 'demo'], floor=0), EMPTY, random.Random(k)).kind == 'demo' for k in range(50))
assert all(check_for(AttrDict(ways=['words', 'analogy'], floor=0), EMPTY, random.Random(k)).kind == 'short' for k in range(50))
```

An idea with no ways, or with no way that a walk can show, gets a short
answer, never a code check. With `hands=False` (the walk has its share
of hands-on checks), an idea gets a short answer in one of its text
ways, else in any text way.

``` python
assert all(check_for(AttrDict(ways=w, floor=0), EMPTY, random.Random(k)).kind == 'short' for w in ([], None, ['timeline']) for k in range(50))
assert all(check_for(AttrDict(ways=['code', 'maths'], floor=0), EMPTY, random.Random(k), hands=False).way == 'maths' for k in range(20))
assert all(check_for(AttrDict(ways=['demo'], floor=0), EMPTY, random.Random(k), hands=False).kind == 'short' for k in range(20))
```

``` python
ml_ = temp_learning(); ml_.put('Ranking', 'Order items by a score.', 'ml')
for m, k in (('code', 'solid'), ('code', 'fragile'), ('maths', 'gap')):
    ml_.record('ranking', f'{m} {k}?', final=True, method=m, outcome=k); ml_.credit_method(m, 'ml', k); time.sleep(.01)
inc = ml_.stats()
test_eq(ml_.method_stats()['methods'], inc.methods)
assert methods_text(inc, 'ml').startswith('Ways that work for you: code 2 of 2')
```

## The profile

What abhyasa knows about you: your background, goals, interests, the
examples that help you, your pace, and what confuses you.

The tutor asks better questions when it knows the learner. A coder gets
code examples. A Sanskrit reader gets a Sanskrit example. This module
keeps one `profile` document on the learning shelf. The profile gets
data in three ways: a short first conversation, edits by the learner,
and changes that the tutor makes from evidence. The module keeps each
change with who made it and why. So the learner can see each change and
undo it. The profile stays in the vault on this machine.

### The fields

A field is a list of short items, or one value. `PACES` names the three
paces. `EXAMPLES` names the kinds of example a learner can like.

[`profile_text`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#profile_text)
gives the profile as lines for a prompt. It is empty when the profile
has no data. So the prompt for a new learner does not change.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1335"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

``` python
def profile_text(
    p
)->str:
```

*The profile as prompt lines; empty when nothing is known.*

[`clean`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#clean)
makes a value fit its field. A list field takes a list or lines of text.
The pace must be a known pace. The session length stays between 3 and
40.

### The tutor learns from evidence

[`observe`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#observe)
reads the recent answers: right or not, confidence, hints,
misconceptions and think-aloud. A small model call proposes at most
three changes, each with its reason.
[`observe`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#observe)
applies them immediately and keeps each one with its reason. So the
learner sees them and can undo them.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1438"

[`observe`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#observe)
applies the changes. A list field takes
[`add`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#add) and

The pace takes `value`. The goals and the notes are for the learner

[`observe`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#observe)


*Change the profile from the recent answers. Return the changes, each

### Who the words are for

Each text that explains an idea is for a human, and humans differ. One
learner is new to the idea, and another knows it well. A text that only
says the definition again teaches little to both. So each teaching
prompt gets two more parts:

- `teach.human`, one shared prompt with the rules on how to teach. It
  comes from the research on how people learn: adapt to the level (the
  expertise reversal effect), a concrete case before the abstract rule
  (concreteness fading), worked steps for a new learner, an analogy with
  its limits, the reason why, and the common wrong idea.
- [`level_line`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#level_line),
  one short line on how well this learner knows the idea now. It comes
  from the learner model: the state of the idea
  ([`understanding`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#understanding)),
  the reasons it is weak, the needs that are not in place, and the
  profile.

The rules say what to do for each level. Shaky, a gap or a missing need:
keep it simple, one idea at a time, a concrete case first, step by step.
Solid: be short, with the exact terms and fewer worked steps.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1476"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### teach_sp

``` python
def teach_sp(
    name:str
)->str:
```

*The prompt `name` with the shared rules on how to teach (`teach.human`)
after it.*

[`level_line`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#level_line)
turns the learner model into one short line. A need is a prereq or a gap
that is not at depth 3 yet; a walk can give its own list in `missing`.
The profile adds the background, the examples that help, the pace and
what confuses them.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1501"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>


*The level line of concept `c` (a slug or a dict) for this learner, with
the needs on the shelf and, unless `profile=False`, the profile. A
question takes no profile: it uses the real terms of the subject.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1484"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### level_line

``` python
def level_line(
    c, by:dict=None, p:NoneType=None, missing:NoneType=None
)->str:
```

*One short line on how well the learner knows concept `c` now, for a
teaching prompt: the state and why, the needs that are not in place, the
profile, and what to do. ’’ with no concept.*

A new idea with no profile asks for the simple form.

``` python
test_eq(level_line(dict(name='Dot product')), "The learner's level on this idea: new to this idea. So: keep it simple.")
test_eq(level_line(None), '')
```

A solid idea asks for the short form, with its depth.

``` python
import time as _t
```

``` python
solid = dict(name='Dot product', floor=4, seen=5, stability=30, last=_t.time())
test_eq(level_line(solid), "The learner's level on this idea: solid, at the apply level. So: be short.")
```

A need that is not in place makes it simple, even for an idea that is
not weak. The profile adds its lines.

``` python
by = dict(dot=dict(slug='dot', name='Dot product', floor=1))
l = level_line(dict(name='Attention', prereqs=['dot'], floor=3, seen=2, stability=30, last=_t.time()), by, dict(background=['writes Python'], pace='gentle'))
assert 'Needs that are not in place yet: Dot product.' in l and 'Background: writes Python.' in l and l.endswith('So: keep it simple.')
```

A gap that the learner named, and an idea with misses, say why they are
weak.

``` python
assert 'a gap' in level_line(dict(name='Softmax', provenance=[dict(src='gap')]))
assert 'shaky (missed the last 2 times' in level_line(dict(name='Softmax', floor=1, seen=3, misses=2))
```

[`teach_sp`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#teach_sp)
puts the shared rules after a prompt.

``` python
assert teach_sp('profile.observe').endswith(prompt('teach.human')) and 'Never only say the definition again' in HUMAN
```

[`plainly`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#plainly)
makes a text that the tutor wrote plain. It is rupaka’s
[`plain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#plain)
when the setting `checks.readable` is on: a text that fails rupaka’s
`plain_why` is written again once, and the new text stays only when it
is better. Each place that shows a model text to the learner uses it.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1509"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### plainly

``` python
def plainly(
    ask, x, terms:tuple=(), keep:tuple=()
):
```

*`x` (a text, or a dict of texts) through rupaka’s
[`plain`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#plain)
with the model `ask`, when `checks.readable` is on; else `x`.*

A plain text makes no model call. A hard text makes one call, and the
plainer text stays. With the setting off, nothing changes.

``` python
calls = []
def fake_ask(p, sp=''): calls.append(p); return 'In a DDPM, the amount of noise at each step is set before training. Which DDPM rule breaks when the network learns it?'
hard = 'You ask the network to learn the noise recipe as it trains. Why does this depart from a DDPM simplifying assumption?'
test_eq(plainly(fake_ask, 'The cat sat.'), 'The cat sat.'); test_eq(calls, [])
assert plainly(fake_ask, hard).startswith('In a DDPM') and len(calls) == 1
set_val('checks.readable', False)
try: test_eq(plainly(fake_ask, hard), hard)
finally: set_val('checks.readable', True)
```

### How well you know what you know

A good learner knows what they know. When you feel sure and you are
often wrong, you stop checking your own thinking. When you feel unsure
and you are often right, you hold back ideas that work. The “Sure?”
choice on each answer gives the data.
[`calibration`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#calibration)
counts the first try of each question. It counts how many times you felt
sure (60% or more), and how many of those answers were right. It counts
the same for unsure. An answer with no confidence, a “don’t know” and a
demo do not count.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1514"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### calibration

``` python
def calibration(
    lr:__main__.Learning, n:int=300
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict:
```

*How often the first try of a question was right, when you felt sure and
when you felt unsure.*

[`calibration_text`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#calibration_text)
gives the calibration in plain words, with one line about what it means.
With fewer than five answers, it gives an empty text.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1527"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### calibration_text

``` python
def calibration_text(
    r
)->str:
```

*The calibration `r` in plain words; empty with fewer than five
answers.*

### Tests

A new shelf has an empty profile, and its prompt text is empty.

``` python
from abhyasa.models import Fake
```

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
p = lr.profile()
test_eq((p.known, p.pace, p.background, profile_text(p)), (False, 'steady', [], ''))
```

`set_profile` keeps each change, with who made it. Lines of text become
a list.

``` python
ch = lr.set_profile(background='codes in Python\nknows Sanskrit grammar', pace='gentle')
test_eq([c['field'] for c in ch], ['background', 'pace'])
p = lr.profile()
test_eq((p.known, p.background, p.changes[0]['by']), (True, ['codes in Python', 'knows Sanskrit grammar'], 'you'))
assert 'Background: codes in Python; knows Sanskrit grammar' in profile_text(p) and 'Pace: gentle' in profile_text(p)
```

When a value stays the same, `set_profile` makes no change. A bad pace
becomes `steady`, and the session length stays in its range.

``` python
test_eq(lr.set_profile(pace='gentle'), [])
test_eq((clean('pace', 'warp'), clean('session_len', '200'), clean('session_len', 'x')), ('steady', 40, 12))
```

`undo_profile` puts back the old value, and keeps the undo as a change.

``` python
cid = [c for c in lr.profile().changes if c['field'] == 'pace'][0]['id']
lr.undo_profile(cid)
test_eq((lr.profile().pace, lr.profile().changes[0]['why']), ('steady', 'you undid a change'))
```

Two changes in one save can have the same time. Each change has its own
id, so the undo changes only the one that you pick.

``` python
import time as _t
```

``` python
real = _t.time
_t.time = lambda: 1000.0   # every change of this save gets the same time
try: lr.set_profile(pace='fast', session_len=20)
finally: _t.time = real
two = lr.profile().changes[:2]
test_eq(two[0]['at'], two[1]['at'])
lr.undo_profile([c for c in two if c['field'] == 'pace'][0]['id'])
test_eq((lr.profile().pace, lr.profile().session_len), ('steady', 20))
```

[`onboard`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#onboard)
fills fields from the answers with one model call.

``` python
fake = Fake({'make a short learner profile': dict(goals=['understand LLM papers'], examples=['code', 'maths'], session_len=8, pace='steady', notes='')})
ch = onboard(lr, fake, dict(want='LLMs, to read papers', how='code please'))
p = lr.profile()
test_eq((p.goals, p.examples, p.session_len), (['understand LLM papers'], ['code', 'maths'], 8))
test_eq({c['by'] for c in ch}, {'onboarding'})
```

[`observe`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#observe)
changes the profile from attempts and keeps the reason. It drops a
change to a field that it must not change.

``` python
lr.put('Attention', 'Weights from query-key dot products.', 'ml')
lr.record('attention', 'What shape is QK^T?', answer='d by d', correct=False, confidence=80, depth=3, misconception='mixes up the axes', final=True)
fake.rules['You keep a short profile'] = dict(changes=[dict(field='confuses', add='tensor shapes in attention', why='You missed a shape question with high confidence.'),
                                                     dict(field='goals', add='hack the planet', why='no')])
ch = observe(lr, fake)
test_eq([c['field'] for c in ch], ['confuses'])
test_eq((lr.profile().confuses, lr.profile().changes[0]['by']), (['tensor shapes in attention'], 'tutor'))
assert 'misconception: mixes up the axes' in fake.calls[-1][0]
```

With no answers there is no evidence, and no model call.

``` python
n = len(fake.calls)
test_eq(observe(temp_learning(), fake), [])
test_eq(len(fake.calls), n)
```

[`calibration`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#calibration)
counts the first try of each question. A pass after a wrong try counts
as wrong. A “don’t know” and an answer with no confidence do not count.

``` python
kl = temp_learning(); kl.put('Attention', 'Weights from query-key dot products.', 'ml')
def rec(q, ok, conf, **kw): kl.record('attention', q, correct=ok, confidence=conf, session='s1', **kw)
rec('q1', False, 90, final=False); rec('q1', True, 90, final=True)   # sure, but wrong on the first try
rec('q2', True, 90); rec('q3', True, 30); rec('q4', False, 10)
rec('q5', False, None, dont_know=True); rec('q6', True, None)
test_eq(calibration(kl), dict(sure=2, sure_right=1, unsure=2, unsure_right=1))
test_eq(calibration_text(calibration(kl)), '')                       # four answers: too few to say
```

With enough answers, the text gives the counts and one line about what
they mean.

``` python
test_eq(calibration_text(AttrDict(sure=4, sure_right=1, unsure=1, unsure_right=0)),
        'When you felt sure, you were right in 1 of 4. When you felt unsure, you were right in 0 of 1. '
        'You are often sure and wrong. Before you answer, ask: how could this be wrong?')
assert calibration_text(AttrDict(sure=1, sure_right=1, unsure=4, unsure_right=4)).endswith('Trust your first idea a little more.')
```

[`evidence`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#evidence)
reads the full conversation of a question. It gets the first error from
a nudge, and the ideas that you said you did not know. It also gets a
lesson that you asked for, the method, and each thing you said.

``` python
el = temp_learning(); el.put('Neuron', 'z = w . x + b.', 'ml')
th = [dict(who='you', text="I don't know what the loop means"), dict(who='tutor', kind='nudge', text='A loop adds products.', first_error='You use squares.'),
      dict(who='you', text='2(w1x1 + w2x2 + b)')]
el.record('neuron', 'Why does z double?', answer='2z', final=True, outcome='fragile', method='maths', thread=th, gaps=['weighted sum as a loop'], taught=1, teach_method='code')
ev = evidence(el)
for s in ('taught with maths', 'first error: You use squares.', 'said they did not know: weighted sum as a loop', 'asked for a lesson after it (code)', "I don't know what the loop means / 2(w1x1"):
    assert s in ev, s
```

[`observe`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#observe)
keeps the calibration in the stats document. So each new question can
read it, and does not have to read all attempts.

``` python
observe(el, Fake({'keep a short profile': dict(changes=[])}))
test_eq(set(el.stats().calib), {'sure', 'sure_right', 'unsure', 'unsure_right'})
test_eq((clean('explore', 'often'), clean('explore', 'always')), ('often', 'sometimes'))
```

`clear_profile` removes the full profile and its list of changes.

``` python
lr.clear_profile()
test_eq((lr.profile().known, lr.profile().changes), (False, []))
```

## Background jobs

One stored row for each background job: what runs, what ended, and where
to see it. The activity chip, the event stream and the Mac app read
these rows.

abhyasa does slow work in the background: it looks for sources, makes a
walk from a link or a goal, files a folder, plans a course, and writes
the notebook of a step. Each such job has one row here. A row has a
`kind`, a `state` (`running`, `done`,
[`failed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#failed),
`stopped` or `closed`), a
[`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#said) line, the
`start` and `end` times, a `title`, and a `url`: the page of its object.

The rows are in vishalakshi’s job `Ledger` (`Vault.ledger`), a table in
the vault file, so they survive a restart. This module is thin glue over
it, with the names that the blocks use. The pool future of a job stays
in memory; the row is the truth for the pages. At a start, each row that
still says `running` becomes `closed`: no job lives across a restart.

Each running job has Stop. Stop asks the job to end at its next safe
point, and the job ends as “You stopped it.” A job that keeps its inputs
on its row (`again`) has Do it again when it ended: the block that runs
it starts the same job with the same inputs.

The rows live in the vault file, next to the concepts and the walks.

### The row

`ENDED` are the states of a job that does not run. `FRESH` is how long
an ended job shows in the activity chip, until you open its page. `KEEP`
is how long an ended row stays at all: the ledger deletes it at the next
start of a job.

abhyasa 0.0.15 kept all the rows in the meta of one document
(`abhyasa:jobs:all`). The first read of the ledger moves those rows to
it one time, and forgets the document. A row that said `running` is
`closed`, as its job did not live across the restart. A row that abhyasa
cannot read is left out: an old row never stops the app.

### Start, end, and a pool job

[`job_start`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#job_start)
writes a running row. `obj` is the object of the job, such as
`walk:<id>` or `course:<id>`; its page marks the end as seen. `quiet`
keeps a job out of the chip, such as the research of a side walk of a
talk.
[`job_end`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#job_end)
closes it. `again` keeps the inputs that start the same job again, for
Do it again. A new start clears the Stop of the last run.

### Stop and Do it again

vishalakshi’s ledger has the state `stopped`, but no way to ask a job to
stop. So abhyasa keeps the ask on the row:
[`stop_job`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#stop_job)
writes `halt`. The job looks at it at its safe points
([`check_stop`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#check_stop)),
such as between two model calls or two pages. A model call that runs
when you press Stop can end, but the job uses no result of it: it ends
as `stopped`, with the line `STOPPED`.
[`JobStopped`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#jobstopped)
is a `BaseException`, so an `except Exception` in the job does not catch
it.

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1613"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### can_again

``` python

    r

```

*Whether the job row `r` ended and kept the inputs (`again`) that start
it again.*

[`track`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#track)
gives a pool future its row: running now, then `done` or
[`failed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#failed)
when it ends. `ok` maps the result to more fields of the row, such as
the link of the walk that the job made, or `state='failed'` for a job
that ended with nothing. `fut` can also be a function that submits the
job: [`track`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#track)
calls it after the row starts, so a fast job never writes to a row that
is not there yet. A row that ended before its future, such as a job that
you stopped, keeps its state. A job that you stopped and that ends with
no safe point after Stop also ends as `stopped`: its result is not used.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1625"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### track

``` python
def track(
    lr:__main__.Learning, key:str, fut, kind:str, ok:NoneType=None, why:NoneType=None, again:dict=None, **kw
):
```

*Start the row `key` of the pool future `fut` (or of the future that the
function `fut` gives), and end it when the future ends:* `ok(result)`
gives more fields (and can set `state`), `why(error)` the line of a
failure. A row that ended first stays. After Stop, the row ends
`stopped`. `again` keeps the inputs for Do it again. Return the future.

A job that runs long says what it does now.
[`job_said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#job_said)
writes a new line to a running row.
[`Said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#said) is the
state of one pool job, and a new
[`said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/show.html#said) goes to
its row too, so a page that reads the row sees the step. Each new line
is also a safe point: after Stop, the job ends there.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

<a
href="https://github.com/vedicreader/abhyasa/blob/main/abhyasa/learner.py#L1641"
target="_blank" style="float:right; font-size:smaller">source</a>

### Seen, closed, and the activity

Opening the page of an object marks its ended jobs as seen. At a start
of the app, a row that says `running` has no job any more: it becomes
`closed`.

``` python

```

changed.*

[`activity`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#activity)
is what the chip lists: each job that runs, then each ended job that is
not seen and less than `FRESH` old. A job that you stopped shows too, so
its Do it again is near. (vishalakshi’s `Ledger.activity` leaves stopped
jobs out, so abhyasa reads the rows itself.) A quiet job never shows.

### Tests

A temporary vault for the tests.

A job starts with a running row and no end; the row is in the chip.

``` python
lr = temp_learning()
r = job_start(lr, 'walk:w1:research', 'research', title='Softmax', said='Finding sources', url='/w/w1#sources', obj='walk:w1')
test_eq((r.state, r.end, r.key), ('running', None, 'walk:w1:research'))
test_eq([x.key for x in activity(lr)], ['walk:w1:research'])
test_eq(chip_words(activity(lr)), '1 running')
```

Its end is news until you open the walk.

``` python
v = job_version(lr)
job_end(lr, 'walk:w1:research', said='2 of 3 ideas have a source')
assert job_version(lr) > v
test_eq(chip_words(activity(lr)), 'Ready: Softmax')
test_eq(seen_jobs(lr, 'walk:w1'), 1)
test_eq(activity(lr), [])
```

An old end and a quiet job do not show. A job that you stopped shows, so
you can do it again.

``` python
job_start(lr, 'k2', 'build', title='Old'); job_end(lr, 'k2')
test_eq(activity(lr, now=time.time() + FRESH + 1), [])
job_start(lr, 'k3', 'research', title='Talk', quiet=True)
job_start(lr, 'k4', 'research', title='Mine'); job_end(lr, 'k4', 'stopped')
test_eq([x.key for x in activity(lr)], ['k4', 'k2'])   # k2 is new now, k4 ended last; k3 is quiet
lr.put_job('k4', seen=True)
test_eq(job_end(lr, 'nope'), None)
```

A restart closes each running row, and the chip says so.

``` python
job_start(lr, 'k5', 'build', title='Diffusion')
test_eq(close_jobs(lr), 2)   # k3 and k5
test_eq(lr.job('k5').state, 'closed')
test_eq(chip_words(activity(lr)), 'Stopped: Diffusion and 1 more')
```

[`track`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#track) ends
the row of a pool future: `done` with the fields of `ok`, or
[`failed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#failed)
with the line of `why`. `ok` can also make it
[`failed`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#failed).

``` python
import threading
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
```

``` python
pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(1)
track(lr, 'b1', pool.submit(lambda: 'w9'), 'build', ok=lambda jid: dict(url=f'/w/{jid}', obj=f'walk:{jid}'), title='A link').result()
pool.shutdown(wait=True)
test_eq((lr.job('b1').state, lr.job('b1').url, lr.job('b1').obj), ('done', '/w/w9', 'walk:w9'))
pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(1)
f = track(lr, 'b2', pool.submit(lambda: 1 / 0), 'build', why=lambda e: 'No walk.', title='Bad')
pool.shutdown(wait=True)
test_eq((lr.job('b2').state, lr.job('b2').why), ('failed', 'No walk.'))
pool = ThreadPoolExecutor(1)
track(lr, 'b4', lambda: pool.submit(lambda: None), 'demo', ok=lambda d: None if d else dict(state='failed', why='No demo.'), title='Late').result()
pool.shutdown(wait=True)
test_eq((lr.job('b4').state, lr.job('b4').why), ('failed', 'No demo.'))   # a function that submits; `ok` sets the state
pool, gate = ThreadPoolExecutor(1), threading.Event()
f = track(lr, 'b5', lambda: pool.submit(gate.wait, 5), 'sort', title='Sort')
job_end(lr, 'b5', 'stopped'); gate.set(); f.result(); pool.shutdown(wait=True)
test_eq(lr.job('b5').state, 'stopped')   # you stopped it: its late end does not make it done
```

A new line of a running job goes to its row.

``` python
job_start(lr, 'b3', 'build', title='Paper', said='Reading the paper…')
st = Said(lr, 'b3', said='Reading the paper…')
st.update(said='Reading 2 of 3 pages…')
test_eq((st.said, lr.job('b3').said), ('Reading 2 of 3 pages…', 'Reading 2 of 3 pages…'))
test_eq((job_said(lr, 'b3', 'Reading 2 of 3 pages…'), job_said(lr, 'nope', 'x')), (False, False))   # no change, no row
```

An ended row older than `KEEP` goes at the next start of a job.

``` python
lr.put_job('b2', end=time.time() - KEEP - 1)
job_start(lr, 'b6', 'build', title='Next')
assert lr.job('b2') is None and lr.job('b3') is not None
```

A slow fake job does three steps, with a safe point before each. Stop
while it does the first step: it ends at the next safe point.

``` python
pool, done, at, go = ThreadPoolExecutor(1), [], threading.Event(), threading.Event()
def slow():
    for k in range(3): check_stop(lr, 's1'); at.set(); go.wait(5); done.append(k)
    return 'made'
f = track(lr, 's1', lambda: pool.submit(slow), 'demo', title='Slow', again=dict(slug='softmax'))
at.wait(5)   # it does the first step
test_eq((stop_job(lr, 's1'), halted(lr, 's1')), (True, True))
go.set(); pool.shutdown(wait=True)
test_eq((done, type(f.exception())), ([0], JobStopped))
```

The stopped job says so, in the chip too.

``` python
test_eq((lr.job('s1').state, lr.job('s1').said), ('stopped', STOPPED))
assert 's1' in activity(lr).attrgot('key')
test_eq(stop_job(lr, 's1'), False)   # it does not run now
```

A job with no safe point after Stop ends `stopped` too, and the fields
of its result do not go on the row.

``` python
pool, gate = ThreadPoolExecutor(1), threading.Event()
f = track(lr, 's2', lambda: pool.submit(lambda: (gate.wait(5), 'w1')[1]), 'build', ok=lambda jid: dict(url=f'/w/{jid}'))
stop_job(lr, 's2'); gate.set(); pool.shutdown(wait=True)
test_eq((lr.job('s2').state, lr.job('s2').url), ('stopped', ''))
```

A new line of a job that you stopped is a safe point:
[`Said`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#said) ends
the job there.

``` python
job_start(lr, 's3', 'build', title='Paper')
st = Said(lr, 's3'); stop_job(lr, 's3')
try: st.update(said='Reading 1 of 3 pages…'); raise AssertionError('no stop')
except JobStopped: pass
test_eq(lr.job('s3').state, 'stopped')
```

Do it again: the stopped job kept its inputs, so it can run again. A job
with no inputs, or a job that runs, cannot.

``` python
test_eq((can_again(lr.job('s1')), lr.job('s1').again), (True, dict(slug='softmax')))
test_eq((can_again(lr.job('s2')), can_again(None)), (False, False))
job_start(lr, 's1', 'demo', title='Slow', again=dict(slug='softmax'))   # the same job again
test_eq((can_again(lr.job('s1')), halted(lr, 's1'), lr.job('s1').halt), (False, False, False))   # it runs, and the last Stop is gone
```

An old jobs document of abhyasa 0.0.15 moves to the ledger at the first
read. Its running row is `closed`, its other rows keep their state, and
a row that is not a dict is left out. The document goes, so the move is
one time.

``` python
old = temp_learning()
rows = {'walk:w7:research': dict(kind='research', state='running', title='Old walk', start=time.time() - 60, obj='walk:w7'),
        'build:b7': dict(kind='build', state='done', title='Old link', start=time.time() - 90, end=time.time() - 30, url='/w/w7', seen=False),
        'bad': 'not a row'}
old.v.add('The background jobs of abhyasa.', title='abhyasa jobs', source=OLD, kind='jobs', meta=dict(rows=rows))
test_eq((old.job('walk:w7:research').state, old.job('build:b7').url, old.job('bad')), ('closed', '/w/w7', None))
test_eq(sorted(old.jobs()), ['build:b7', 'walk:w7:research'])
assert old.v.by_source(OLD) is None   # the old document is gone
test_eq(chip_words(activity(old)), 'Stopped: Old walk and 1 more')   # the closed row ended last
```

A jobs document with meta that is not JSON of rows does not stop the
app: it has no rows, and it goes.

``` python
odd = temp_learning()
odd.v.add('The background jobs of abhyasa.', title='abhyasa jobs', source=OLD, kind='jobs', meta=dict(rows='not a dict'))
test_eq(odd.jobs(), {})
assert odd.v.by_source(OLD) is None
```

## Stored walks

> A walk is a vault document of kind `journey`. This part reads and
> saves it, finds the current idea, and counts the steps for the rail.

The planner that makes a walk is in `abhyasa.path`. The tutor, the web
app and Leela read a walk with the names here.

### The document

A walk is one vault document of kind `journey`. Its meta has the goal, a
title, a subject, and the steps. Each step has a slug, a status (`todo`,
`known` or `skip`) and the reason that it is in the path.

### Change a step, read the rail

`walk_step` merges changes into one step and saves the walk.
`merge_journey` merges changes into the fields of the walk, such as
`sitting`. Both hold the lock of the walk
([`keyed_lock`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#keyed_lock),
one lock for each kind and key), so two requests on one walk do not lose
a change.
[`walk_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#walk_state)
gives each step a dot for the rail: `done` (outcome `solid`), `shaky`
(outcome `fragile`, `gap` or `misconception`), `skipped`, `known`, `now`
(the first step with no outcome and the status `todo`) or `todo`.

The sections of a walk from a paper or a link follow the document: a new
document or a new section name starts a section. A walk from a topic or
a goal has no source document (`source` is empty). Its sections are the
sections of the plan (the `section` of a step), so a passage from
another document does not start a section, and “Section done” shows only
at the end of a plan section.

### Learning.walk_slug

``` python
def walk_slug(
    jid:str, slug:str, **kv
)->fastcore.basics.AttrDict | None:
```

*Merge `kv` into the step on concept `slug` of walk `jid`, wherever it
is now, under the lock of the walk. None when the walk or the step is
gone. A job that runs while you move steps uses this, never a place.*


*The steps with a `dot`, the index of the current step, the counts, and
the sections as `(name, [indexes])`. With `by` (slug -\> concept),* a
step on a concept that you learned in a session or in another walk is
`known`, with `elsewhere`, and it is not the current step.

### keyed_lock

``` python
def keyed_lock(
    kind:str, key, rlock:bool=True, weak:bool=False
):
```

*The one lock of `key` in `kind` (such as a walk id or a concept slug),
so that two writers of one thing take turns. With `rlock`,* the thread
that holds it can take it again. With
[`weak`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#weak), a
lock that no caller holds goes away: use it only with `with`.

[`keyed_lock`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/learner.html#keyed_lock)
gives one lock for each kind and key. The same kind and key give the
same lock, and another kind gives another lock. A weak lock goes away
when no caller holds it:

``` python
import gc
```

``` python
a = keyed_lock('walk', 'k1'); test_is(keyed_lock('walk', 'k1'), a); test_ne(keyed_lock('concept', 'k1'), a)
test_eq(type(keyed_lock('concept', 'k2', rlock=False)), type(threading.Lock()))
with keyed_lock('open-q', 'q1', weak=True): assert ('open-q', 'q1') in _WEAK
gc.collect(); assert ('open-q', 'q1') not in _WEAK
```

`walk_slug` finds the step by its concept. A step that moved still gets
the change, and a step that left the walk gets nothing.

``` python
ws = temp_learning(); ws.put_journey(dict(id='wsl', title='W', mode='walk', steps=[dict(slug='a'), dict(slug='b')]))
test_eq(ws.walk_slug('wsl', 'b', note='N').steps[1]['note'], 'N'); test_is(ws.walk_slug('wsl', 'zz', note='N'), None)
```

With `by`,
[`walk_state`](https://vedicreader.github.io/abhyasa/agent_tools.html#walk_state)
reads the concepts too. An idea that you learned in a session or in
another walk is `known (learned elsewhere)`: it counts as done, and the
current step is the next idea that you do not know.

``` python
kn = temp_learning(); kn.put('A', 'a', 'ml'); kn.put('B', 'b', 'ml'); kn.update('a', floor=4, seen=1)
kj = dict(id='k', source=None, steps=[dict(slug='a', status='todo'), dict(slug='b', status='todo')])
test_eq(walk_state(kj).current, 0)   # with no concepts, step a is still to do
ks = walk_state(kj, {c.slug: c for c in kn.concepts()})
test_eq([s.dot for s in ks.steps], ['known', 'now']); test_eq((ks.current, ks.done, ks.steps[0].elsewhere), (1, 1, True))
```
